# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **TSMC booked $5.10 billion in foreign subsidies, funding fabs from Arizona to Nanjing.**

**What You Need to Know:** TSMC booked $5.10 billion in foreign subsidies, funding fabs from Arizona to Nanjing. The nine-month haul, NT$167.586 billion from the United States, Japan, Germany and China, landed almost entirely in the third quarter and is tied to property, construction and tools at the overseas subsidiaries. Arizona’s second fab is scheduled for 3-nanometer mass production in the third quarter of 2027.

### Top Story
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing’s Friday financial report puts combined subsidies from the United States, Japan, Germany and China at NT$167.586 billion (US$5.10 billion) for the first nine months of this year, a record for that stretch and cover for property purchases, plant construction and production equipment. The third quarter alone was NT$166.996 billion, after NT$590 million in the first half. The recipients are TSMC Arizona, European Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. in Dresden, Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing in Kumamoto, and TSMC Nanjing, each under agreements with local governments. Nanjing runs a 12-inch wafer fab. Arizona’s first fab began commercial production in the fourth quarter of 2024 on 4-nanometer; construction of the second fab is complete, equipment installation is underway, and mass production is scheduled for the third quarter of 2027 on 3-nanometer. Kumamoto’s first fab began commercial production at the end of 2024, with a second fab under construction for mass production in 2028; Dresden is scheduled to begin mass production next year. Over the nine months, TSMC Arizona posted a profit of NT$53.986 billion and JASM a profit of NT$2.396 billion, while ESMC reported a loss of NT$1.079 billion. Source: [focustaiwan.tw](https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202611140005)
Source: [taiwannews.com.tw](https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/6476352)

### Silicon
**South Korea Expects Nvidia GPU Deliveries Under Contracts to Continue: TokenPost**
South Korea’s government expects Nvidia GPU deliveries covered by signed contracts to continue through the chipmaker’s leadership change, and it put a deployed count on the buildout: about 13,100 Nvidia B200 GPUs are already in the country. Plans to introduce next-generation GPUs, including Vera Rubin, are expected to proceed as planned. Nvidia’s work in South Korea spans AI data centers, autonomous driving and robotics, with NAVER, Hyundai Motor Group, SK Telecom and Kakao Mobility. The industry minister had given a similar assurance on November 9 that contracted deliveries would not be disrupted; this statement added the B200 count and the next-generation plans. Source: [tokenpost.com](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/technology/57187)

**Penguin Solutions Introduces CXL-Enabled DDR4 Module for AI Data Centers: HPCwire**
Penguin Solutions introduced the SMART CXL-8F2W-D4, an eight-DIMM DDR4 Compute Express Link memory add-in card that lets organizations adapt prior-generation DDR4 for use in AI systems. The Fremont company describes it as validated reuse that offers performance, cost savings, and another path to procuring memory for AI infrastructure buildouts. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/penguin-solutions-introduces-cxl-enabled-ddr4-module-for-ai-data-centers/)

**Staera Semiconductor Emerges from Stealth with $4.6M to Break AI’s Data Bottleneck: HPCwire**
Staera Semiconductor, formerly New Silicon Corporation, emerged from stealth with $4.6 million and a method that builds LED optical data links directly into silicon chips. The San Francisco company is aiming the links at AI systems that need to move data faster and scale further without adding power or heat. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/staera-semiconductor-emerges-from-stealth-with-4-6m-to-break-ais-data-bottleneck/)

**Intel’s ISA Reference Confirms Razor Lake Desktop and Laptop Model IDs: TechPowerUp**
Intel’s November Architecture Instruction Set Extensions Programming Reference, revision 063, adds Razor Lake and Coral Rapids. Razor Lake gets four model values under family 18 (12H), the same family as Nova Lake: 12_06H and 12_0AH for desktop, 12_07H and 12_09H for laptops. Coral Rapids Xeon is 13_08H, after Diamond Rapids at 13_01H. InstLatX64 spotted the update. Razor Lake picks up SSBD_PSFD_U_S, described as separate user-mode and supervisor-mode control over certain speculative memory behavior; both families gain APIC-Timer Virtualization; Coral Rapids adds VPMLDSABFLYDQ, aimed at ML-DSA. GCC patches posted this week give Razor Lake the same ISA feature set as Nova Lake, which should mean AVX10.2 and APX carry over, while Coral Rapids stays on AVX10.2 rather than AVX10.3 for now. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354804/intels-isa-reference-confirms-razor-lake-desktop-and-laptop-model-ids)

### Data Centres & Power
**European Union offers to build data center for Moldova: Data Center Dynamics**
The European Union has offered to build a data center for Moldova, proposed by enlargement commissioner Marta Kos on a visit last week, to help protect citizens’ personal data from cyberattacks. If accepted, the facility would be built with assistance from Sweden, Europa Libera reported. Prime minister Vasile Tofan welcomed the offer and said preparatory work is advancing for a secure data center and a stronger link to the European artificial intelligence ecosystem. The offer came at the first meeting of the High-Level Digital Connectivity Platform in Chișinău. The European Commission said the summit’s purpose was to invest up to €623 million ($689 million), pledged by nations and private-sector partners, in digital connectivity between Europe and Central Asia, including 5G, space-based connectivity and data center infrastructure in the Black Sea region, Turkey and the southern Caucasus. A separate Logos Press estimate put the sum required to build a government facility consolidating public digital services at €50 million ($55 million). The offer follows an October 2026 cyberattack that exposed personal data of an estimated 450,000 Moldovan citizens. DataCenterMap lists six facilities in the country, all in Chișinău. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/european-union-offers-to-build-data-center-for-moldova/)

**NTT Docomo to pilot data center heat-reuse for on-shore shrimp farm in Japan: Data Center Dynamics**
NTT is set to pilot waste heat from a data center to warm an on-land shrimp farm, under a Tokyo Metropolitan Government program for unused data-center heat. IMT Engineering and NTT Docomo announced “Construction of a Waste Heat Utilization Type Land-Based Aquaculture System,” starting next year with heat from an NTT Docomo Business data center in or near Tokyo and running until March 2028. Recovered heat will warm rearing water for Pacific white shrimp, a use NTT framed for waste heat that has been hard to apply because it is relatively low temperature. Hibiya General Equipment will design and build the heat-recovery and supply gear; NTT Green & Food, formed in 2023 with Regional Fish, will run the aquaculture and judge whether production costs fall. The four firms want a model that can move to other data centers. Elsewhere in the same city program, KDDI and ElleThermo are deploying a self-powered temperature sensor that can generate electricity from heat around 20–40°C, and Kratwerk and Tokyu Construction are taking waste heat from a small modular data center under a railway overpass for server cooling. NTT Docomo’s Nexcenter sites are seven around Tokyo, one in Yokohama, two in Osaka, one in Kagawa, one in Shanghai and two in Hong Kong. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/ntt-docomo-to-pilot-data-center-heat-reuse-for-on-shore-shrimp-farm-in-japan/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**GlobalFoundries Breaks Ground on First New Semiconductor Fab Under Landmark U.S.-Japan Initiative: TechPowerUp**
GlobalFoundries broke ground on the first new semiconductor manufacturing facility planned for its Malta, New York, site under a U.S.-Japan initiative: a 300-millimeter fab pairing Japanese investment with GF’s technology and manufacturing, aimed at automotive, industrial and connected-infrastructure demand. On October 14, GF said it was selected as technology provider and operator for two new fabs at Malta, under an initiative providing up to $21 billion. Japan provides the investment; GF contributes differentiated technologies and operations. An initial investment of about $10 billion, with $570 million in New York State incentives, is accelerating the first fab, expected online in 2029. About $10 billion more is set for a second fab as the project advances. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354803/globalfoundries-breaks-ground-on-first-new-semiconductor-fab-under-landmark-u-s-japan-initiative)

**Chinese AI labs are training models on Nvidia’s Blackwell despite export controls, says ex-OpenAI engineer: The Register**
A November 12 forensic analysis from Will DePue, a former OpenAI engineer now at Unemployment Labs, reports that six Chinese models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group were initialized on Nvidia Blackwell systems, four of them matching Grace Blackwell GB200 and GB300 configurations in Nvidia’s liquid-cooled rack-scale lineup. The names every account agrees on are DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3 and MiniMax-M3; shattered.io says the models date from April 2026 onward, unlike earlier Chinese releases that matched Hopper. DePue said he searched more than six trillion combinations of chip layout and seed number against open weights, and that initialization traces survive into published models. The Register says this is the first public link of MiniMax and Ant Group to Blackwell, and that the report includes seeds tying DeepSeek-V3 to Hopper and DeepSeek-V4-Flash to Blackwell. The method identifies the hardware used to set initial weights, not where those chips sat, who owned them, or whether the rest of training stayed on Blackwell; a lab could have initialized through a U.S. provider. DePue said senior researchers inside and outside frontier labs, including OpenAI and Anthropic, confirmed the result. Separately, Israel-based Lava reported 32 Nvidia B300 GPUs, Blackwell Ultra parts under U.S. export controls, through publicly exposed monitoring endpoints with IP addresses geolocated to China. DePue also said Unemployment Labs is raising $5 million for six more months of research. Source: [theregister.com](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/11/13/chinese-ai-labs-are-training-models-on-nvidias-blackwell-despite-export-controls-says-ex-openai-engineer/5309891)
Source: [shattered.io](https://shattered.io/chinese-ai-models-nvidia-blackwell-depue-six-models-location-unknown/)

**Instead Of Lowering GPU Prices, Former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Reportedly Financed AI Startups To Absorb Excess Silicon: Wccftech**
The Wall Street Journal, as reported by Wccftech and TechPowerUp, describes an August 2026 meeting in which Colette Kress, then chief financial officer and now interim chief executive, pushed to rein in circular financing to smaller cloud providers and to OpenAI and Anthropic. Initial discussions had floated underwriting roughly 8 gigawatts of OpenAI compute valued at up to $250 billion; Kress scaled the signed guarantee to roughly 4.25 gigawatts, or up to $125 billion. Huang reportedly called her “a deer in the headlights.” To justify underwriting buyers, he privately admitted major cloud companies were pivoting to in-house chips and that prepaid TSMC wafers and memory were “coming at him like an avalanche.” Funding data-center buildouts for AI startups, the report says, created demand to clear surplus silicon rather than let it force GPU prices down. Analyst Ed Zitron has estimated that at least $200 billion of Nvidia AI GPUs sit idle in warehouses after cloud purchases that lacked grid capacity or immediate demand. Nvidia reportedly then contacted TSMC to wind down upcoming chip orders. Source: [wccftech.com](https://wccftech.com/jensen-huang-financed-ai-startups-absorb-excess-silicon/)
Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354814/nvidia-allegedly-engineered-scarcity-by-funding-ai-startups-to-buy-its-gpus)

**US lawmakers push for tighter chip export controls on China as Jensen Huang resignation controversy grows: Zaobao**
After Jensen Huang’s resignation, House Speaker Mike Johnson said on November 12 that he favors limiting China’s access to advanced chips and sees a developing consensus in Congress. Republican chairs of three House committees urged that four chip-control bills go into the annual National Defense Authorization Act. Three are already in the Senate version: more congressional oversight of advanced-chip export policy, a requirement that manufacturers track where advanced chips go, and pressure on allies to restrict sales of advanced chipmaking equipment and related maintenance. The fourth, the Remote Access Security Act, would let Commerce restrict Chinese companies from renting controlled Nvidia chips at overseas data centers; the House passed it in January and it awaits the Senate. The same chairs asked Huang to appear for closed-door questioning on December 1 and to confirm in writing by November 13 or face a subpoena. Attorney General Todd Blanche said the FBI is investigating allegations that Alice Huang worked for the Chinese government, and that the Justice Department has not determined she was a spy. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Friday that China opposes abuse of export controls that disrupts supply chains. Bloomberg, citing people familiar, said Manhattan federal prosecutors are investigating whether companies linked to Huang Le smuggled Super Micro Computer products into China, and that Justice is also examining Megaspeed International. Malaysia’s investment, trade and industry ministry said it is working with customs on whether AI chips imported by Speedmatrix, Megaspeed’s Malaysian subsidiary, were re-exported. Since July last year Malaysia has required prior approval to export, re-export or transit high-performance U.S. AI chips. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said there is currently no indication that AI chips linked to Megaspeed had been moved out of Malaysia. Source: [zaobao.com.sg](https://www.zaobao.com.sg/en/news/world/us-lawmakers-push-tighter-chip-export-controls-china-jensen-huang-resignation-controversy-grows)

### Also Today
**Nvidia board reportedly approached Arm CEO Rene Haas during replacement search: Tom’s Hardware**
Nvidia’s board approached Arm chief executive Rene Haas, a long-time Nvidia veteran, during the search for a replacement chief executive. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/gpus/nvidia-board-reportedly-approached-arm-ceo-rene-haas-during-replacement-search-jensen-huangs-transgressions-leave-nvidia-scrambling-to-fill-a-massive-void)

**Shifting HBM4 Controller Functions Closer To Memory (UC Riverside): Semiconductor Engineering**
Tharunya Yogananda and Wantong Li of the University of California, Riverside, published a paper on partitioning the HBM controller across the host and the HBM base die, noting that recent generations such as HBM4 let that base die be manufactured on a logic process. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/shifting-hbm4-controller-functions-closer-to-memory-uc-riverside/)

### The Teardown: The Copy After Every Layer
A training step is arithmetic plus a copy, and the copy is what infra.bea.ai times when it asks whether a consumer GPU can stand in for a data-center accelerator. The guide puts an RTX 4090 at 82.6 teraflops of BF16, then draws three gaps compute does not close: 24 gigabytes of memory against 80, an interconnect of 32 gigabytes per second against 900, and no error-correcting memory where training expects it. Parameters, optimizer state and activations all have to live in that 24 gigabytes. The link has to move a slice of those numbers after every layer if the model is split across cards. PCI Express is the only path on a consumer board. There is no NVLink, so tensor-parallel all-reduce cannot hide inside a dedicated GPU fabric.

Take the guide’s 7-billion-parameter case, sharded across eight 4090s. With a micro-batch of one, a sequence length of 2048 and full checkpointing, activations are about 2 gigabytes and the running total is 18 gigabytes. Headroom is 6 gigabytes. That remainder is the budget for a longer sequence. At 4096 tokens the same card needs gradient checkpointing and a micro-batch of one. Extra sequence length is not a software preference. It is the memory that is left after weights and optimizer state have taken their share.

The interconnect numbers show why adding cards does not refill that budget. Tensor-parallel all-reduce has to finish after every layer. infra.bea.ai times it at 640 milliseconds on PCI Express and 22 milliseconds on NVLink. If the forward and backward pass takes 500 milliseconds, the PCI Express copy more than doubles the step. Fully sharded data parallel does not dodge the wire: an all-gather at the start of each layer and a reduce-scatter at the end add about 900 milliseconds on PCI Express to a 7-billion-parameter step that would spend about 32 milliseconds on the fast link. Eight cards therefore buy eight small memories and a bus that spends more time synchronizing than the arithmetic spends computing.

That design stops being the right one when either budget is gone. When sequence length consumes the 6 gigabytes of headroom, another 4090 does not create one larger address space. When the 640-millisecond all-reduce exceeds the 500-millisecond compute step, another card adds a participant to the copy, not a shorter step. The 82.6 teraflops still sit on the board. They wait on 32 gigabytes per second, and on 24 gigabytes that cannot see the other 24. Source: [infra.bea.ai](https://infra.bea.ai/guide/distributed/parallelism-planning/consumer-gpu-feasibility/)

### On the Horizon
- TSMC’s second Arizona fab is scheduled to begin 3-nanometer mass production in the third quarter of 2027; Dresden is scheduled to begin mass production next year, and Kumamoto’s second fab in 2028.
- GlobalFoundries’ first new Malta fab is expected online in 2029.
- House committee chairs asked Jensen Huang to appear for closed-door questioning on December 1, 2026, with written confirmation due November 13.
- NTT Docomo’s Tokyo-area shrimp-farm heat pilot is set to start next year and run until March 2028.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Six hundred megawatts of Texas power has a hyperscaler check, and Fermi's biggest lease is dead.**

**What You Need to Know:** An unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler is funding 600 megawatts of power at Fermi's planned Project Matador campus in Texas, while the TensorWave lease is terminated. Nscale's new prospectus puts active GPUs at 50,000 and active and contracted capacity at 1.37 gigawatts. OpenAI has told lawmakers it will back bills meant to tighten advanced-chip exports to China.

### Top Story
Fermi has a deal with an unnamed investment-grade hyperscaler to develop 600 megawatts of power at planned Project Matador in Texas, with that power to start coming online next year. The customer is providing $200 million up front and $15 million under an early construction and site-development agreement, and the two sides are finalizing a $90 million purchase of structural steel and long-lead building materials Fermi had already secured. No lease is signed; Fermi says the client is making financial and development commitments ahead of a lease so power stays on the customer's schedule. The same update ends the August 2026 TensorWave lease, which had been set for up to 650 megawatts and carried AMD credit support, so Matador is again without a tenant. Fermi still describes a possible 17-gigawatt campus near Amarillo on Texas Tech University system land, and chief executive Lee McIntire said converting the current pipeline into leases would fill 2.2 gigawatts of capacity the company already counts. For the three months to the end of September, Fermi reported a $141.6 million net loss, and debt stood at $958.4 million. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/fermi-does-600mw-power-deal-with-hyperscaler-but-tensorwave-lease-is-officially-dead/)

### Silicon
**Kioxia and Dell Build a 157 PB Rack With 640 SSDs: TechPowerUp**
Kioxia and Dell have put 157 petabytes of raw flash in one 42U rack, running Dell ObjectScale on 16 PowerEdge R7725xd servers that together hold 640 of Kioxia's 245.76-terabyte LC9 SSDs. Each 2U server takes 40 E3.L drives, the same layout the two showed in May at 9.8 petabytes per server, so the 16 servers occupy 32U and leave 10U free. The LC9 parts are PCIe 5.0 NVMe drives on Kioxia's eighth-generation BiCS FLASH QLC with a 32-die stack; the full 245.76-terabyte capacity is only in the E3.L form factor. The 2.5-inch and E3.S versions top out at 122.88 terabytes, which would cut a rack built the same way to about 78.6 petabytes. Dell's George Papadopoulos said the point is to consolidate data into fewer systems and racks and cut cabling, power, and cooling. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354767/kioxia-and-dell-build-a-157-pb-rack-with-640-ssds)

**Axelera AI Unveils Titania Architecture Ahead of SC26: HPCwire**
Axelera AI, based in Eindhoven, has unveiled Titania, a third-generation chiplet architecture it says is aimed at the racks enterprises and labs already own. The company describes it as delivering the performance of a data-center-grade server at a cost and power budget below an RTX 6000 server. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/axelera-ai-unveils-titania-architecture-ahead-of-sc26/)

**AMD Expands Instinct MI400 GPU Portfolio for HPC and AI for Science: HPCwire**
AMD is adding detail to the Instinct MI400 series, spanning scientific computing and AI. It is sharing more on the MI430X, introducing the MI450X on the Helios rack-scale system, and reporting a measured inference result it calls a leadership figure for the MI455X on Helios. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/amd-expands-instinct-mi400-gpu-portfolio-for-hpc-and-ai-for-science/)

### Data Centres & Power
**Nscale brings online two data centers and 25,000 GPUs in 2.5 months: Data Center Dynamics**
Nscale has brought two more data centers and about 25,000 GPUs online since August 31, taking active GPUs to 50,000 of a planned 461,000. The August 31 prospectus had listed 25,000 active GPUs, about five percent of the goal; active sites are now seven, up from five that then carried 55 megawatts, with ten more in the pipeline. Active and contracted capacity is 1.37 gigawatts: 1 gigawatt at owned sites, 200 megawatts at leased sites, and 165 megawatts in colocation, with what the company calls a line of sight to 10 gigawatts. The new prospectus reports full-year 2025 revenue of $33 million, up 73 percent from $19.1 million in 2024, after an earlier prospectus had put the six months to the end of June 2026 at $140.6 million of revenue and losses of $1.02 billion, against $368.9 million a year earlier. Active total contract value is $6.4 billion, and active plus contracted TCV is $105.8 billion, compared with $0.5 billion and $38.0 billion at December 31, 2025, under long-term take-or-pay contracts tied to those 461,000 GPUs. Anthropic has exercised a right to more compute in Building 2 at the Monarch campus in West Virginia, on top of the $45 billion agreement signed in August; Nscale expects to fund that build with external financing and operating cash flow, and a missed GPU timeline can let Anthropic end that tranche without liability. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/nscale-brings-online-two-data-centers-and-25000-gpus-in-25-months/)

**STTGDC launches 22MW data center in Noida, India: Data Center Dynamics**
STTGDC has energized a 22-megawatt data center, NOI2, in Noida, Uttar Pradesh. Indian neocloud Neysa is set to lease capacity there and place about 9,000 GPUs in the building. Noida 1 offers 17 megawatts, and Noida 3 is under development at 28 megawatts; the company first announced Noida plans in 2021. STTGDC's India division counts more than 600 megawatts of critical IT load in operation and development across 34 facilities in ten cities. KKR and Singtel fully acquired STT GDC in February and have rebranded it STTGDC. India chief executive Bimal Khandelwal tied the hall to demand for larger, more compute-intensive workloads in the Delhi NCR market. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/sttgdc-launches-22mw-data-center-in-noida-india/)

**Labor Shortages Threaten Data Center Schedules: Data Center Knowledge**
JLL's 2027 US Construction Perspective forecasts national tender prices up 4.2 percent in 2027, from 3.1 percent in 2026, above a pre-2020 norm of 2 to 3 percent, and that projection is for construction broadly, not data centers alone. The South is expected to add more nonresidential construction growth than any other US region and to carry the heaviest workload per worker by 2028, driven by data centers, power projects, and public civil works. JLL's Matthew Giddings said the cost of a crew runs past wages into overtime, travel, lodging, and relocation, and that extra crews can raise cost without raising output if design, materials, and sequencing are not coordinated. He said utility crews for lines and substations and the electrical trades that energize a hall are not interchangeable, and that JLL has seen halls substantially complete, with power available, still months from operation because commissioning staff were not there. Prefabricated electrical assemblies and standard cooling plant cut on-site labor, but the manufacturers of those assemblies have their own staffing limits; Giddings said repeatable campus designs do more than one-off prefabrication, and that overtime does not move an opening date if the constraint is a transformer, utility energization, or commissioning. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/data-center-construction/labor-shortages-threaten-data-center-schedules)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**OpenAI backs US bills to tighten AI chip export controls to China: Chosunbiz**
OpenAI has told US lawmakers it will support a bipartisan package to restrict China's access to advanced AI chips and chipmaking tools, after months of review, Chosunbiz reported from Bloomberg. The three bills would limit exports of advanced AI semiconductors to China, block indirect shipments of Nvidia AI chips, and limit China's access to advanced equipment from ASML; lawmakers want them inside the annual National Defense Authorization Act and passed by year-end. Nvidia and related trade groups have opposed tighter controls. Jensen Huang, who had opposed stricter China rules, resigned on November 12, and the report says that has weakened Nvidia's position on Capitol Hill. The outcome is still open: Congress and the administration are negotiating the text, and a Trump veto signal could collapse the effort. Source: [biz.chosun.com](https://biz.chosun.com/en/en-it/2026/11/13/KJPZBL3ZMFB45AJNF432WNZG3A/)

**ViTrox Reports Nearly 200 AI-Powered X-Ray Inspection Systems Deployed: Semiconductor Digest**
ViTrox says nearly 200 of its V810Ai QX1 automated X-ray systems have been deployed within one year at major global AI-server manufacturers. The machine is specified at 2 micrometre resolution and plus or minus 50 degrees of tomography, with AI defect classification and an optional dual-lane layout, for flip-chip and system-in-package boards. On the optical side, the V510Ai ST inspects boards up to 600 by 510 millimetres at up to 64 centimetres per second. The tools feed ViTrox's V-ONE manufacturing-intelligence layer, including ONE View image checks at buy-off and Process Insight ticketing when a defect condition trips. ViTrox is showing the line at SEMICON Europa in Munich, November 10 to 13. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/vitrox-reports-nearly-200-ai-powered-x-ray-inspection-systems-deployed/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=vitrox-reports-nearly-200-ai-powered-x-ray-inspection-systems-deployed)

### Also Today
**HyperAccel to Showcase LPU-Based AI Inference System at SC26: HPCwire**
South Korean fabless firm HyperAccel will show an eight-LPU server and run a live remote demonstration of its language-model processing unit. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/hyperaccel-to-showcase-lpu-based-ai-inference-system-at-sc26/)

**AMD "Siren Halo" APU Rumored to Pair Dedicated GDDR7 With LPDDR Memory: TechPowerUp**
TechPowerUp reports a November 12 post credited to Gotou_3rd claiming AMD's unconfirmed Siren Halo keeps LPDDR system memory and adds a dedicated GDDR7 pool. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354765/amd-siren-halo-apu-rumored-to-pair-dedicated-gddr7-with-lpddr-memory)

**Nvidia confirms planned supply of GPUs to S. Korea despite Huang's resignation: science minister: The Korea Times**
The Korea Times reports that Nvidia has confirmed planned GPU supply to South Korea will continue despite Jensen Huang's resignation, according to the science minister. Source: [koreatimes.co.kr](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/business/20261113/nvidia-confirms-planned-supply-of-gpus-to-s-korea-despite-jensen-huangs-resignation-science-minister)

### The Teardown: One Pass Across the Wafer
A line-scan camera does not frame a wafer. It holds one row of pixels in the optical field, and motion turns each readout into the next strip of the map. Semiconductor Digest, covering SEMICON Europa, reports Teledyne Vision Solutions demonstrating that geometry on a 300-millimetre wafer with the Linea ML 32K, which Teledyne calls the world's first true 32K line-scan camera, inspecting the wafer in a single pass at 10 micrometre resolution.

The row has to span the diameter, or the tool is back to stitching. A second swipe adds travel, an overlap band, and a seam the defect software must not call a crack. Teledyne's width claim rests on two figures that sit on different planes of the same lens. The Linea ML 32K is specified at 32K resolution with 2.5 micrometre pixels. The Munich demonstration inspects at 10 micrometres on the wafer. The 2.5 micrometre number is the photosite. The 10 micrometre number is the patch of silicon that photosite represents in this setup. When the wafer-side patch is coarser than the photosite, the lens is folding a wide strip onto that long sensor, and a 32K row is the sample count Teledyne is using so the strip covers a 300-millimetre wafer without a second index.

Pace lives on the same row. The camera is rated at imaging speeds of up to 150 kilohertz, so it can emit up to 150,000 lines a second while the stage moves. In this demonstration each new line is one step of the 10 micrometre grid. That rate is the budget for stage speed before pixels smear, and it is also the budget for the other modes Teledyne lists on the Linea platform: multiline operation, high dynamic range, and time-delay integration. Multiline and TDI spend successive readouts on the same feature so a faint scratch or a thin resist edge collects more signal before the image is committed. HDR holds a bright pad and a dark neighbourhood in one line. Those modes do not widen the sensor. They spend the 150 kilohertz. A line that must run at the full rate for throughput is not, in that same pass, banking a long TDI sum.

The demonstration walks in four steps, all of them Teledyne's figures. The wafer is 300 millimetres across. The inspection grid in the single-pass demo is 10 micrometres. One line is a 32K sensor whose photosites are 2.5 micrometres, so optical scale, not a second mechanical pass, is what fits the diameter into the row. That row is clocked at up to 150 kilohertz so the stage can keep feeding lines without stopping to reposition. Width from the 32K line, scale from the 10 micrometre grid, pace from the 150 kilohertz rating: that is the single-pass claim.

The Z3 on the same stand is a different instrument. Semiconductor Digest lists spatial resolution up to 1.25 micrometres, height repeatability up to 35 nanometres, and throughput up to two seconds per wafer. The jobs named for it are micro ball-grid arrays, bumps and pillars, through-glass and through-silicon vias, wafer-to-wafer bonding, flatness, coplanarity, and defect analysis, on a die, a wafer, or a stretch frame. A 10 micrometre line can show that a bump is missing or far from its pad. It cannot certify a height error at the Z3's 35-nanometre repeatability, because that error is a sliver of the lateral pixel.

Single-pass 32K imaging loses the job when the scrap signature is vertical: bump height, via depth, bond-line tilt, a coplanarity stack. Then the two-second Z3 measurement is the step that closes the lot, and another swipe of the line camera only reprints a map that was already wide enough. The demonstration is in Hall C2, Stand 136, at Messe München, November 10 through 13. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/teledyne-vision-solutions-demonstrates-single-pass-300mm-wafer-inspection/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=teledyne-vision-solutions-demonstrates-single-pass-300mm-wafer-inspection)

### On the Horizon

- JLL says tender prices typically trail input costs by three to six months, so increases through late 2026 continue to show up in bids in early 2027.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Seventeen degrees in fifteen seconds: Waterloo's droplets cut simulated hotspots for data-centre cooling.**

**What You Need to Know:** University of Waterloo researchers reported a hybrid cooler that uses tiny drops of coolant to cut simulated chip hotspots by up to 17°C in 15 seconds, aimed at cooling AI data centres more effectively and economically. Malaysia is weighing a law that would make data-centre builders declare operators, sites and GPU import counts. TSMC confirmed a cloud-vendor leak of about 46,000 employee records and said production was untouched.

### Top Story
University of Waterloo researchers are developing a hybrid cooling method that puts tiny drops of coolant on chip hotspots, HPCwire reported on November 12. The method cut the temperature of simulated chip hotspots by up to 17°C in 15 seconds. The group says data centres at the centre of the AI buildout could be cooled more effectively and economically with the system, which is still under development. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/waterloo-researchers-develop-hybrid-cooling-method-for-chip-hotspots/)

### Silicon
**AMD Announces 6th Gen EPYC Embedded 9006 Series Processors: AMD**
AMD announced the 6th Gen EPYC Embedded 9006 Series on the SP7 socket, built on Zen 6. The line goes up to 256 cores and adds PCIe Gen 6 and CXL 3.1 connectivity. AMD is offering seven-year product longevity for the embedded parts. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/AMD/status/2120532173623054816)

**Compal Unites NVIDIA Compute and Networking at SC26: HPCwire**
Compal will show NVIDIA-based AI servers at Supercomputing 2026, November 17–19, at Booth 5008 in McCormick Place, Chicago. The lineup includes the air-cooled SGX30-2 and the direct liquid-cooled OG430-2-L1 on NVIDIA HGX B300, plus the OG231-2-L1 accelerated server with NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8, with NVIDIA MGX and RTX PRO called out for enterprise AI and visual computing. Compal will also show the NVIDIA Vera CPU Compute Tray, and for clusters the NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPU, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC and Spectrum-6 Ethernet switches. Its Daxi AI Server Manufacturing Center in Taiwan opened in August 2026, alongside manufacturing investments in Texas and Vietnam. Alan Chang, vice president of Compal's Infrastructure Solutions Business Group, said high-speed interconnects and integrated system architectures are essential to scaling AI infrastructure efficiently. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/compal-unites-nvidia-compute-and-networking-at-sc26/)

**This is the Meta MetaRoCE Network Adapter: ServeTheHome**
ServeTheHome reported that Meta showed its MetaRoCE network adapter at OCP Summit 2026. The adapter is designed to scale to million-GPU training clusters. Source: [servethehome.com](https://www.servethehome.com/this-is-the-meta-metaroce-network-adapter/)

### Data Centres & Power
**Struggling marijuana farmers pivot to becoming AI data center sites: Tom's Hardware**
In Arizona, former dispensary owner Moe Asnani told Arizona Public Media that cultivation is being abandoned and that existing grow houses could be reused as mini data-centre nodes, after state cannabis sales peaked in 2024 and oversupply pushed prices down. Forbes described a 32,850-square-foot cannabis facility in Kalamazoo, Michigan, wired for 1.5 megawatts, expandable to 2.5 megawatts in under a year and to 15 megawatts longer term, with fibre and HVAC already in place. Tucson City Council member Paul Cunningham said reusing buildings that already drew that power and water is more acceptable than a new data centre on the edge of town, and the piece said even OpenAI and Anthropic are interested in smaller sites as large campuses draw opposition. Niki Krear of New Lake Capital Partners told MJBizDaily that operators want affordable power, dense fibre and favourable tax policy together. The same account said data centres often need two to three times the power a grow already has, that upgrades can take up to five years, and that smaller sites face zoning, moratoriums, neighbour opposition and higher per-unit upgrade prices because suppliers discount large orders. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/cannabis-farmers-consider-joining-ai-bandwagon-due-to-falling-weed-revenue-existing-sites-could-house-mini-data-center-nodes-but-still-face-serious-challenges-during-conversion)

**Energy storage firm Torus launches prefabricated modular data center product, raises $500m: Data Center Dynamics**
Energy-storage firm Torus launched a prefabricated modular data-centre product, Torus Foundry. It raised $500 million to scale that product. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/energy-storage-firm-torus-launches-prefabricated-modular-data-center-product-raises-500m/)

**Chatsworth Products Showcases Rack, Power, and Cooling Solutions for AI and HPC at SC26: HPCwire**
Chatsworth Products, based in Simi Valley, California, said it will show infrastructure for AI and high-performance computing at SC26. The showcase includes its OCP Open Rack V3, previews of upcoming power and cooling products, and integrated liquid-cooling gear for high-density rooms. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/chatsworth-products-showcases-rack-power-and-cooling-solutions-for-ai-and-hpc-at-sc26/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Malaysia moves to tighten data centre controls amid scrutiny over Nvidia chip exports: The Vibes**
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the government is considering a law that would make companies planning data centres declare their operators, facility locations and the number of GPUs they intend to import, so chips under US export controls stay in domestic use and are not diverted. He said the country must not be used for what is defined as an illegal transaction. Malaysia introduced export controls last year on the movement of high-performance AI chips of US origin. Johari said there are no plans to investigate Speedmatrix, the Malaysian subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed, because he does not see a law that applies if GPUs are bought for the buyer's own data centres; Megaspeed chairman and chief executive James Tan Yong Pong said, in a statement Reuters cited, that the firm takes US export-control duties seriously and will cooperate with Washington. Johari said trade and Taiwanese investment continue, Malaysia has followed the One-China policy since 1974, and both sides remain willing to negotiate under a 1993 agreement. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim told the Dewan Rakyat the postponed sessions were the Economic Cooperation Committee, the Trade Working Committee and the Investment Working Committee, not all trade and investment talks, and that Kuala Lumpur has already asked for those meetings to resume. Source: [thevibes.com](https://www.thevibes.com/articles/news/129471/malaysia-moves-to-tighten-data-centre-controls-amid-scrutiny-over-nvidia-chip-exports)

**TSMC confirms employee data leak as hackers seek 3 BTC for the records: Crypto Briefing**
TSMC said on November 12 that personal data on some current and former employees was exposed through a third-party cloud system, and that its internal systems, wafer production and customer data were not breached. Hackers listed about 46,000 records totalling 6.9 GB on DarkForums and BreachForums for 3 bitcoin, about $220,000 or NT$7.4 million, and threatened to publish the set if it was unsold within a week. A sample file named tsmc.txt held 499 records with 19 fields, including names, national IDs, home addresses, phone numbers, emails, bank information, job titles and emergency contacts. TSMC said the leaked content matches a partner cloud system, and that it is notifying affected people and working with the vendor, law enforcement and outside cybersecurity firms. The Taiwan Information Security Association told Current Weekly the records could support phishing and longer-term poaching of advanced-process staff. In June 2023 LockBit demanded $70 million after hitting hardware supplier Kinmax rather than TSMC's own network; KuCoin noted TSMC's third-quarter 2026 net profit of NT$763.064 billion, with advanced-process revenue at 79 percent. Source: [cryptobriefing.com](https://cryptobriefing.com/tsmc-employee-data-leak-3-btc/) · [kucoin.com](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/hacker-demands-3-btc-for-6-9gb-of-tsmc-employee-data-claims-leak-from-cloud-vendor)

**Jensen Huang's affair with alleged spy revives push to tighten China chip curbs ahead of Trump-Xi summit: CNBC**
Days before President Donald Trump is due to meet Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 18–19, CNBC reported that the Jensen Huang scandal is strengthening lawmakers who want the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act and the MATCH Act written into this year's National Defense Authorization Act. Semafor reported that China this week extended the current truce until January, and Bloomberg analyst Michael Deng, a former Commerce Department official, said Beijing will know Trump may not be able to hold commitments he makes. The Information, cited by CNBC and by Yahoo Finance, says the Commerce Department is finalizing a rule to stop Chinese AI firms from remotely using advanced chips in data centres outside China. CNBC, citing The Information, said Alice Huang helped facilitate at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to China, and it cited a May Culper Research estimate that more than 20 percent of Nvidia revenue for the year ended July 2025, about $43.2 billion, came from China through illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries. Paul Triolo of DGA-Albright Stonebridge Group said Chinese officials have been clear they will answer passage of the MATCH Act, including by tightening controls on rare earths and magnets. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in September that negotiators had taken export controls off the table as a national security issue; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday he wants a constructive relationship based on balance and reciprocity; Trump said Sunday he did not know whether Huang would join the trip but would certainly take him. Source: [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/12/nvidia-trump-jensen-chip-export-controls-china-xi-.html) · [semafor.com](https://www.semafor.com/article/11/12/2026/nvidia-fallout-could-hamper-us-china-trade-talks) · [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/u-finalizing-rule-block-china-042215614.html)

### Also Today
**Chinese universities obtain Nvidia chips despite US export controls: Digitimes**
Reuters, as carried by Digitimes, reported that several Chinese universities, including Northwestern Polytechnical University, one of China's Seven Sons of National Defense, have obtained Nvidia chips despite US export controls. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261112PD237/chips-nvidia-university-supplier-military.html)

**Hardware-Based Location Checks Target AI Chip Smuggling (Texas A&M): Semiconductor Engineering**
Texas A&M researchers published a paper, “5G CATS: 5G-Based Cryptographic Authorization Against Trafficking of Semiconductor Devices,” arguing that round-trip time to a trusted landmark can bound where an AI accelerator is operating after it ships, though jitter in honest replies forces the verifier to loosen that bound. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/hardware-based-location-checks-target-ai-chip-smuggling-texas-am/)

### The Teardown: The Voltage Where Delay Bends
Near threshold, a transistor sits so close to the voltage where it just begins to conduct that a small sag in the supply stretches delay much more than the same sag would on a normal rail. Semiconductor Engineering's November 12 account of edge-AI system-on-chip design places that regime at about 0.4 to 0.5 volts in advanced FinFET processes. Energy per operation falls as the rail falls. Dynamic energy tracks the square of voltage, so the same switching activity on a lower rail spends sharply less energy. What arrives with that saving is delay that grows rapidly, device-to-device variation that widens, and noise margins that shrink. Timing paths become sensitive to small voltage changes. IR drop and local voltage droop become first-order effects. A guard band drawn from nominal-voltage behaviour stops predicting the silicon, and models taken at the nominal voltage no longer describe the part.

Memory is often the floor under that rail. A single-rail memory with silicon-validated assist features can support operation down to about 600 millivolts, which lets the designer take the V-squared energy cut without splitting the power grid. A dual-rail memory separates the logic supply from the memory supply so compute can drop further while the array stays where it still holds state. Semiconductor Engineering points to an ISSCC 2025 result: a dual-rail SRAM at 38 megabits per square millimetre, logic at 380 millivolts and the memory rail at 540 millivolts, built in a 3-nanometre FinFET. Ultra-low-power register files hold local data next to compute. The split of jobs follows the block. Multiply-accumulate tiles want small, distributed SRAM. Activation units want those register files with wide data paths. Shared system buffers want a high-bandwidth AXI interface.

Logic libraries have to be built for the bend in the curve, not borrowed from a nominal-voltage deck. The account calls for moment-based LVF timing and noise models across a wide process-voltage-temperature range, delay and slew models that capture the nonlinear sensitivity near threshold, and extra checks for MIS effects, pulse-width integrity, skew interactions and mixed-device behaviour, because noise margins are thinner. Silicon validation, including extended timing and functional sweeps, is what keeps those models honest. I/O is the quiet veto on the whole plan. Control interfaces such as GPIO, I3C, I2C and SWI3S, high-speed links such as LVDS and RGMII, clock and reference inputs, SD and eMMC, test I/O, and 2.5D or 3D integration I/O for chiplets each have to run consistently across the supplies the core wants. If the periphery cannot, it sets the system minimum voltage, and the core's near-threshold work never appears in the product.

A closed loop among foundation IP, EDA tools and silicon feedback is what the account says makes operation around 0.4 to 0.5 volts predictable. Memories, cell libraries and I/Os have to be chosen and validated early. The near-threshold rail stops being the right choice when the memory or the I/O cannot follow the compute supply down, or when the extra delay and variation force guard bands that hand back the energy the lower voltage was meant to buy. In that case a dual-rail split, or a rail held above the sharp part of the delay curve, is what keeps a real-time edge workload inside its timing budget. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/designing-edge-ai-socs-at-near-threshold-why-foundation-ip-can-help-you-break-down-the-power-wall/)

### On the Horizon
- Supercomputing 2026 runs November 17–19 in Chicago, where Compal is booked at Booth 5008 and Chatsworth Products plans to show Open Rack V3 and liquid-cooling gear.
- President Trump is slated to meet Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on November 18–19, with chip-export language in this year's defense bill still in play.
- The TSMC employee-record listing, posted November 12, carried a one-week deadline before the sellers said they would publish the full set.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **TSMC cleared up to $1 billion for two AI labs, beside $40.93 billion for fabs.**

**What You Need to Know:** TSMC’s board cleared up to $1 billion for OpenAI and Anthropic, set beside about $40.93 billion in manufacturing appropriations. The lab stakes are caps, not completed purchases, and the Anthropic shares are priced off a future IPO. The same meeting also cleared up to $500 million for an unnamed semiconductor-ecosystem vehicle.

### Top Story
On a November 10 statement, TSMC’s board approved buying up to $500 million of OpenAI preferred stock and up to $500 million of Anthropic common shares at the price of a future initial public offering. Those figures are maximums; the full purchases have not been completed, and the Anthropic stake still depends on an IPO and other conditions. At the same meeting the board approved approximately $40.93 billion in capital appropriations for advanced and specialty process capacity, advanced packaging, facilities systems, and research and development, tied to long-term capacity plans based on market demand forecasts. OpenAI and Anthropic run on data-centre processors TSMC already manufactures for Nvidia and other customers, and the proposed stakes stay small next to that manufacturing program. The board also approved third-quarter financial statements and routine capital and personnel matters. Source: [technode.global](https://technode.global/2026/11/11/tsmc-openai-anthropic-investments/) Source: [marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/tsmc-gets-board-nod-to-invest-up-to-500-million-in-proposed-wholly-owned-subsidiary-shares-up-3-ce785edbd889f02d) Source: [marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/tsmc-s-board-approves-nt-9-per-share-q3-dividend-shares-up-3-ce785edbd889f322)

### Silicon
**Arm Congratulates Google Cloud on TPU Portfolio Expansion with Axion CPUs: Arm**
Arm said Google Axion CPUs, which are Arm-based, now power host compute across TPU 8t, TPU 8i, and TPU 8i Max as Google Cloud expands that TPU portfolio. Arm framed the step as CPU and accelerator co-design for large-scale training, real-time reasoning, and agentic workloads. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Arm/status/2120291428123226493)

**ASUS Showcases ProArt GR1X, ProArt P16 and P14, and ProArt OLED Monitors at Adobe MAX 2026: TechPowerUp**
ASUS is showing the ProArt GR1X, a new agentic-AI mini PC, plus ProArt P16 and P14 laptops and ProArt OLED monitors, at Adobe MAX 2026. The GR1X uses a 6144-core NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and up to 128 GB of unified memory, on the RTX Spark stack — CUDA, TensorRT, NVFP4, RTX ray tracing, DLSS, and OptiX — running Windows. ASUS says creators can keep client footage on the machine and iterate without per-token or per-generation fees. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354685/asus-showcases-proart-gr1x-proart-p16-p14-laptops-proart-oled-monitors-and-ai-powered-solutions-for-creatives-at-adobe-max-2026)

**Purdue to Bring Google TPUs to Campus Research Computing: HPCwire**
Purdue University, in West Lafayette, Indiana, said on November 11, 2026 that a collaboration with Google Public Sector, Cirrascale, and DDN will provide Google Tensor Processing Units for faculty and student research. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/purdue-to-bring-google-tpus-to-campus-research-computing/)

### Data Centres & Power
**CoreWeave Q3 2026 Earnings: CoreWeave**
CoreWeave reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $3.7 billion, up 168 percent year over year, and adjusted operating income of $379 million, above its guidance, with double-digit adjusted operating margins a quarter ahead of plan. Active power stands at 1.7 gigawatts-plus, doubling the active footprint year to date. Customer prepayments and deposits in the quarter were roughly $9 billion. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/CoreWeave/status/2120264279245156454)

**Jefferson Lab Decommissions SciPhi-XVI After Nearly a Decade of Physics Research: HPCwire**
Jefferson Lab in Newport News, Virginia, has powered down SciPhi-XVI, also called 16p, after nearly a decade of theoretical-physics work. The machine ranked among the world’s 500 fastest supercomputers when it came online in 2016. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/jefferson-lab-decommissions-sciphi-xvi-after-nearly-a-decade-of-physics-research/)

**How Kazakhstan’s Akashi Data Center is building trust: Data Center Dynamics**
In a sponsored account, Data Center Dynamics reports that Kazakhstan’s Akashi Data Center is leaning on Uptime Institute Tier IV certification, backing from a development bank, and the protections of English common law. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/product-news/how-kazakhstans-akashi-data-center-is-building-trust/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Finetech Expands its Portfolio for Volume Production: Semiconductor Digest**
André Thiemann became co-CEO of Finetech on November 1, alongside CEO Carlotta Baumann, as the Berlin die-bonding supplier pushes packaging processes from the lab into volume manufacturing. The pitch is one hardware and software platform from process development through prototyping to production, without process requalification, aimed at photonics, quantum technology, and semiconductors. Supported bonds include thermocompression, eutectic, adhesive, ultrasonic, laser-assisted, and hybrid bonding, with sub-micron placement accuracy. Thiemann comes from Nikon SLM Solutions, where he led operations strategy and set up a US assembly site. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/finetech-expands-its-portfolio-for-volume-production/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=finetech-expands-its-portfolio-for-volume-production)

**ICsense Reports Record Growth as Demand Rises for Specialized Medical ASICs: Semiconductor Digest**
Belgian chip house ICsense reported a record year, with revenue up 30 percent and profits up by more than 50 percent, driven in part by custom chips for brain-computer interfaces and implantable medical devices. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/icsense-reports-record-growth-as-demand-rises-for-specialized-medical-asics/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=icsense-reports-record-growth-as-demand-rises-for-specialized-medical-asics)

### The Teardown: When the Next Hall Leaves the Hub
Two-thirds of new US data center projects are targeting rural locations, Data Center Knowledge reports, while nearly nine-tenths of the halls already standing remain in developed areas. The installed base and the pipeline are no longer the same map.

Site selection used to stack three tests on top of each other: access to power, proximity to end users, and a high-performance network already in reach. Those tests explain the old concentration in or near cities, and in hubs such as Northern Virginia, Texas, and California. A rural parcel fails the old tests on paper. It sits farther from users, so latency rises, and both power and network gear may be less developed or simply farther away.

Power is the test that moved. Public grids, including grids in wealthy, highly developed regions, cannot always meet what a new data center asks for. Operators are exploring power they generate themselves — dedicated generation assets or an on-site plant. From that angle, a thin local grid stops being a veto. Distance from existing electrical infrastructure becomes something you build around, not a reason to discard the parcel. Land works the same direction: undeveloped urban parcels large enough for a hall are limited and expensive, while many rural markets are less tight. Fewer neighbors can also mean simpler permitting and less organized opposition.

Fiber does not get that waiver. A data center still needs high-performance network infrastructure, which in most cases means fiber-optic cable, and many rural areas have little of it. The cost comparison is what makes the split workable. Extending fiber is typically less expensive and less complex than building long-distance power infrastructure or developing major on-site generation. If fiber already exists within a few hundred miles of the proposed site, connecting to it can be economically viable. On-site generation covers the electrons; a few hundred miles of fiber covers the packets. Neither substitute covers the other.

The two-thirds figure is a pipeline count, not a census of what is already energized. Nearly nine-tenths of existing data centers are still in developed areas, so the industry is not moving the old halls. It is siting the next wave somewhere else. The idea itself is not new. Amazon explored data centers in Chile and Argentina more than eight years ago, and rural siting as a discussion goes back at least a decade. Hyperscalers are again looking at remote parts of South America. What changed is execution: over the past few years, operators have begun breaking ground on rural projects at a greater scale, pulled by power sourcing, land, and community response.

That design choice stops being the right one when the job cannot spend the distance. Halls that need ultra-low latency stay near users. Builds whose scale does not justify the infrastructure spend a remote site requires stay near a grid and a fiber route that already exist. If power, land, and local opposition stay tight, a larger share of the next large projects lands outside the old metro hubs. A workload whose round trip cannot spare those miles never makes that shortlist. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/data-center-site-selection/the-rural-shift-in-data-center-development)

### On the Horizon
- November 17–19, 2026, Chicago: INFINITIX makes its SC26 debut at Booth 6111, showing HPC scheduling in AI-Stack and the ixCSP cloud-operations platform.
- This November at SC26, MGHPCC exhibits at Booth 3255 with more than 75 research projects and the AI Compute Resource, plus a virtual booth.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **TSMC's 17.61 billion dollar October shows AI chip demand still filling the foundry.**

**What You Need to Know:** TSMC's October consolidated revenue reached 17.61 billion dollars, the foundry's clearest monthly print yet that AI chip orders are still filling leading-edge capacity. The month beat August's record, and the company's own fourth-quarter range still implies two more heavy months. Separately, filings described to Bloomberg put Nvidia B300 servers inside China, and that report is now sitting beside a live congressional push on export bills.

### Top Story
TSMC reported October consolidated revenue of NT$586.89 billion, which ANI put at 17.61 billion dollars, up 59.7 percent from October 2025 and 14.7 percent from September's NT$511.86 billion (15.36 billion dollars). Asia Business Daily notes that print cleared the prior monthly record, August's NT$514.81 billion, and puts October near 23.8 trillion won; October 2025 had been NT$367.47 billion, or 11.02 billion dollars. January through October reached NT$4,485.62 billion, about 134.57 billion dollars, up 43.3 percent from 93.91 billion dollars a year earlier. The company's own fourth-quarter forecast remains 52.3 billion to 54.3 billion dollars; the midpoint, 53.3 billion, is 58 percent above the year-ago quarter and 14 percent above the prior quarter, and readers of that range expect November and December each at NT$538.1 billion to NT$569.9 billion. A second Asia Business Daily report, citing United Daily News and CNBC, says the 2-nanometer process has entered mass-production ramp, that 3-nanometer and 5-nanometer demand from NVIDIA, AMD and cloud providers remains strong, and that TSMC is still adding CoWoS capacity. That report also says capital spending for 2026 through 2028 is planned substantially above the prior three years; third-quarter operating margin was 58.7 percent, above the top of the company's 58 percent forecast band, on revenue of NT$1.49 trillion and net income of NT$763.1 billion. Source: [aninews.in](https://www.aninews.in/news/business/tsmc-october-revenue-surges-597-yoy-to-usd-1761-billion20261110150617) Source: [asiae.co.kr](https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026111019165171242) Source: [asiae.co.kr](https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2026111015584317372)

### Silicon
**AMD's RDNA 5 Inches Closer as GFX13 Support Lands in Linux Driver Patches: TechPowerUp**
AMDGPU maintainer Alex Deucher submitted eight patches on November 9 that add GFX13 support to the open-source AMDGPU driver, more than 12,600 lines excluding the usual large headers. The series brings version 13 of the graphics block, the MicroEngine Scheduler, and the IMU, and it names two targets, GFX 13.0.1 and GFX 13.0.4, which are IP configurations rather than product names. On the compute side, AMDKFD gains initial GC 13 support, a CWSR trap handler that saves and restores compute wave state, and a temporary disable of queue reset in the topology. The last patch turns on MGCG, CGCG, and CGLS clock gating so idle blocks draw less power. AMD has not confirmed that GFX13 is RDNA 5; TechPowerUp notes the assumption rests on GFX12 having been tied to RDNA 4. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354637/amds-rdna-5-inches-closer-as-gfx13-support-lands-in-linux-driver-patches)

**Google TPU 8tx Pairs AMD EPYC Turin Hosts with Confidential Computing while TPU 8i Max Doubles Memory Bandwidth: ServeTheHome**
AMD said it has expanded its Google Cloud collaboration so that 5th Gen EPYC processors host Google Cloud TPU 8tx and help protect sensitive AI models. ServeTheHome describes the new TPU 8tx as pairing those EPYC Turin hosts with confidential computing, and says TPU 8i Max doubles memory bandwidth for inference. The posts do not add a wattage, a process node, or a ship count. Source: [servethehome.com](https://www.servethehome.com/google-tpu-8tx-8i-max-amd-epyc-turin/) Source: [x.com](https://x.com/AMD/status/2119781382662570141)

**Infineon Processes Functional Power Devices on 300mm SiC Wafers: Semiconductor Digest**
Infineon has processed 300-millimetre silicon carbide wafers into functional power devices at its fab in Villach, Austria. The result is a process demonstration on the larger wafer, not a stated high-volume shipment. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/infineon-processes-functional-power-devices-on-300mm-sic-wafers/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=infineon-processes-functional-power-devices-on-300mm-sic-wafers)

**Fraunhofer IPMS Highlights Semiconductor Technology Developments at SEMICON Europa: Semiconductor Digest**
Inside the European APECS pilot line, Fraunhofer IPMS has for the first time integrated chiplets into pockets in a silicon wafer, planarized the surface, and prepared it for wafer-level interconnect — the first major milestone on its quasi-monolithic integration roadmap, on work it runs at 200-millimetre and 300-millimetre. Director Wenke Weinreich framed the problem as integrating chiplets that carry memory or photonic functions while validating the processes under industry-relevant conditions, including back-end steps moving into front-end flows. The institute's silicon-nitride waveguide platform, on both wafer sizes, is described as extremely low loss from the visible spectrum into the mid-infrared. Its hafnium-oxide ferroelectric FRAM and FeFET pilot-line devices switch below one volt and in the nanosecond range. The same portfolio is what IPMS will show at SEMICON Europa, alongside FAMES pilot-line work, under the Chips for Europe Initiative. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/fraunhofer-ipms-highlights-semiconductor-technology-developments-at-semicon-europa/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=fraunhofer-ipms-highlights-semiconductor-technology-developments-at-semicon-europa)

**Oklahoma State Expands Regional Research Computing with Cimarron Supercomputer: HPCwire**
Oklahoma State University says Cimarron, operated by its High Performance Computing Center, is now available to researchers across Oklahoma, Arkansas, and Kansas. The machine provides 37,760 processor cores, 392 GPUs, and more than 10 petabytes of storage. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/oklahoma-state-expands-regional-research-computing-with-cimarron-supercomputer/)

### Data Centres & Power
**AI’s Efficiency Challenge For The Semiconductor Industry: Semiconductor Engineering**
John Kibarian's October 15 keynote at PDF Solutions CONNECT, written up today, treats a McKinsey base case as a capacity problem rather than a capital problem: device revenue from 975 billion dollars in 2025 to about 2.3 trillion in 2030, an 83.5 percent rise, with 58 percent of that growth from data centers and servers compounding at 29 percent a year. Installed AI data-center capacity of 45 to 60 gigawatts in 2026 is projected at 100 to 160 gigawatts by 2030. At 150,000 to 200,000 wafers per gigawatt, half of them HBM, that implies 9.6 million to 17.5 million additional wafers and 16 to 29 new fabs sized at 50,000 wafer starts a month; Kibarian notes a modern leading-edge logic fab runs closer to 20,000 starts, which could double the fab count. The same talk puts 2030 AI revenue at 3.9 trillion dollars and margins at roughly 30 million dollars per megawatt, and says a GPU on inference can spend over 90 percent of its power on memory updates and idle time. A manufacturing executive, he said, had already been told he could not get more tools than had been promised, so the only path left was more output from the tools on the floor. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/ais-efficiency-challenge-for-the-semiconductor-industry/)

**Greenpeace projects three chipmakers could use 15 percent of Taiwan's power by 2030: TNGlobal**
Greenpeace projects that three chipmakers could use 15 percent of Taiwan's power by 2030. The projection is a demand forecast for the island's grid, not an energized campus and not a megawatt figure for any one site. Source: [technode.global](https://technode.global/2026/11/10/greenpeace-taiwan-chipmakers-power-demand-2030/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Nvidia’s China Spy Fallout Deepens: Report Says Moonshot AI Accessed NVDA’s Advanced Chips Despite Export Controls: Stocktwits**
Bloomberg, as reported by Stocktwits, says Moonshot AI signed an August contract to rent 32 Super Micro servers equipped with Nvidia B300 GPUs, and that Beijing filings valued those servers at 432 million yuan, 64.8 million dollars, and placed them in China — a possible breach of rules that bar such sales without a license. Moonshot disputed the documents; after Bloomberg asked for comment, they no longer named Moonshot. House Republicans Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford have asked Jensen Huang to a closed briefing and for a reply; Senators Elizabeth Warren and Jim Banks, in a November 9 joint statement, want the AI Overwatch Act in the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has called for a full briefing and tighter controls. Chosun Biz, citing Reuters, says three bills already in the Senate's fiscal 2027 defense package — AI Overwatch, the Chip Security Act, and the MATCH Act, each cleared earlier by the House Foreign Affairs Committee — now have a better chance, that Nvidia is viewed as the strongest opponent of the first two, and that the White House has not taken a position; President Trump said Huang told him he had not known the woman was suspected of being a Chinese spy. In the quarter ended July 26, revenue from customers headquartered in China, including Hong Kong, was 7.9 billion dollars, about 8 percent of total revenue, and Hopper shipments bound for China were less than 1 percent of data-center revenue; Nvidia does not include China data-center compute revenue in its forward outlook. Source: [stocktwits.com](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/nvidia-s-china-spy-fallout-deepens-report-says-moonshot-ai-accessed-nvda-s-advanced-chips-despite-export-controls/cNGua6lR97A) Source: [en.fnnews.com](https://en.fnnews.com/news/202611101118562684) Source: [biz.chosun.com](https://biz.chosun.com/en/en-international/2026/11/10/XK37L5P4CVDZJCSRYLV7C2D3QU/)

**SCHMID to Supply Equipment for Advanced Packaging Facility in South Asia: Semiconductor Digest**
SCHMID has an equipment order for an advanced-packaging facility in South Asia, framed as a step from pilot lines toward volume manufacturing of glass-core substrates for AI and high-performance computing. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/schmid-to-supply-equipment-for-advanced-packaging-facility-in-south-asia/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=schmid-to-supply-equipment-for-advanced-packaging-facility-in-south-asia)

**Micron Supports Workforce Training at SUNY Jefferson with $750K Grant: Micron**
Micron said a 750,000 dollar Community Investment Fund grant is backing SUNY Jefferson's workforce program in the renovated Dulles Building, focused on mechatronics and advanced manufacturing. The first bootcamp class is underway, aimed at students, service members, veterans, military spouses, and military-connected families, toward certifications and college credit for semiconductor manufacturing in New York. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/MicronTech/status/2119836566726316306)

### Also Today
**Deutsche Telekom Expands AI Factory with NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs: The Fast Mode**
The Fast Mode reports Deutsche Telekom is expanding its AI factory with Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs. Source: [thefastmode.com](https://www.thefastmode.com/technology-solutions/51358-deutsche-telekom-expands-ai-factory-with-nvidia-blackwell-ultra-gpus)

**Streaming Scan Network Test Over PCIe: Semiconductor Engineering**
Teradyne has integrated Siemens Tessent Silicon Executable into the UltraPort server and IG-XL on UltraFLEXplus so Streaming Scan Network patterns reach the chip over its own PCIe link, through an on-chip controller on AXI, rather than only through a dedicated test port. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/streaming-scan-network-test-over-pcie/)

**Microsoft Patent Describes Paying PC Owners to Train AI on Idle GPUs: TechPowerUp**
A Microsoft Technology Licensing application, submitted in April 2025 and made public on November 5, describes chopping training jobs into micro-tasks for opted-in phones, laptops, and gaming PCs with spare GPU capacity, with credits redeemable for software, model access, or money — an application, not an announced Windows or Xbox service, and with no payout rate. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354630/microsoft-patent-describes-paying-pc-owners-to-train-ai-on-idle-gpus)

### The Teardown: The Insertion That Cannot See the Next Model
A test insertion used to be a cut the process and the physics already knew how to make. Semiconductor Engineering's account of where AI silicon is now starts from the opposite problem: the workload can change in the time it takes to get the chip out of the building, so the question is no longer only whether a contact is good. It is which slice of the build is still worth a tester hour once the algorithm that justified the die has already moved on.

The path is a chain of partial views. Wafer sort and singulated-die probe can sit at the fab, with that site's test program and its own record of failure mechanisms. The next assembly — a compute die, a stack of high-bandwidth memory, other chiplets, an interposer — is likely an OSAT job, on a different program, and the two data sets do not have to meet. Advantest's Scott Segura describes the physical reason the chain is getting longer: more active parts in the substrate, parts moved closer together, functional test creeping into what used to be a contact check, and performance probe at die level that now has to hold thermals. Known-good die, in that account, has to handle 3 kilowatts while it is still a singulated die. Silicon photonics, already, is five insertions. The substrate those dies land on is leaving the round wafer for a 310 by 310 millimetre panel, chosen so the tools can hold more dies, and that panel test is the step Teradyne's Jeorge Hutarte puts at the OSAT.

Walk the clock against that chain. ChatGPT arrived in November 2022. Widespread commercial use of agentic systems took slightly more than two years — about the time to design, verify, validate, ride a shuttle, package the part, and drop it into a working system. The design cycle those customers are trying to shrink is still 18 to 24 months, and some large chipmakers have told their EDA suppliers they want six. Even if the drawing board hit six months, the fab, the package, and the board would still be staring at a model generation that turned over inside the same window. Segura's customers already tape out, run the model or look at the end application, and then do not ship that chip. They ship a derivative, or a different version. Every insertion written for the first tapeout — the 3-kilowatt singulated probe, the five photonics stops, the panel-level functional test — was aimed at a part the lab may already have walked away from.

The cut stops being the right cut when the failure you still need to catch only exists after the compute die, the memory stack, the interconnect, the firmware, and the software are in one box, and the company holding that box cannot see the wafer-sort mechanisms from the company that probed the die. More insertions then buy contact confidence on a workload that has already left, while the combined behavior the field will actually run sits in a data set the previous insertion never receives. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/test-struggles-to-keep-pace-with-ai/)

### On the Horizon
- November 12: TSMC lists green bonds of NT$14.8 billion, about 450 million dollars, on the Taipei Exchange, as ANI reported via Focus Taiwan.
- November 11: the reply deadline House committee chairs set for Jensen Huang on a closed briefing they asked him to attend on November 18, covering contacts related to the Megaspeed matter and Nvidia's security systems.
