# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Two billion dollars in restricted AI chips are tied to the probe now sitting with NVIDIA's board.**

**What You Need to Know:** Two billion dollars in restricted AI chips are now tied to an independent probe NVIDIA's board has opened around Jensen Huang. Korea's memory makers are spending well above 100 trillion won this year while Yangtze Memory raises the share of domestic tools in new NAND fabs. NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom announced a link that puts Korean-designed processors on NVLink Fusion.

### Top Story
NVIDIA's board is initiating an independent investigation into reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, while Tom's Hardware reports Megaspeed has been accused of smuggling two billion dollars worth of AI chips into China through its subsidiary Speedmatrix. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the inquiry; the board says it has no reason to believe national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, says it has confidence in Huang and his leadership team, and says he supports the review and will cooperate, with further updates as appropriate. TechPowerUp, citing The New York Times, describes a close relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, which is believed to be helping Chinese companies obtain NVIDIA chips barred from shipment to Chinese customers, and says a network of sister companies is building data centers in Malaysia for those customers. Tom's Hardware adds that Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, was allegedly recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, that the suspected operation has not been independently confirmed, and that the relationship is alleged to follow a honeypot approach. Huang wrote that he was unfaithful to his wife, Lori, to whom Tom's Hardware says he has been married for 41 years, that he supports the investigation, and that he is committed to protecting NVIDIA and America's national security; NVIDIA has rejected suggestions of improper dealings, and Chinese officials have dismissed the espionage allegations as unfounded. Tom's Hardware notes Huang has criticized limits on AI GPU supply to China, including calling the "China hawk" label a badge of shame and saying it "doesn't have to be all us or them," drawing fire that included the CEO of Palantir, and that it remains unclear whether he will leave the CEO role as Intel's Brian Krzanich did in June 2018, when Robert Swan became interim chief executive. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354594/nvidia-launches-investigation-into-jensen-huangs-relationship-with-suspected-chinese-spy) Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/gpus/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-admits-to-having-an-affair-with-suspected-chinese-spy-jensen-apologizes-in-letter-to-staff-company-board-forms-independent-committee-to-investigate) Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/statement-from-nvidia-board-of-directors)

### Silicon
**DeepX Tapes Out Second-Gen Chip, Projects 6.7× Performance Gain With LPDDR5x-PIM: EE Times**
DeepX has taped out a second-generation AI accelerator aimed at edge markets including robotics. EE Times reports the part can run large language models on device in under 5 W, and the company projects a 6.7× performance gain with LPDDR5x-PIM. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/deepx-tapes-out-second-gen-chip-projects-6-7x-performance-gain-with-lpddr5x-pim/)

**NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom Announce Collaboration to Advance Sovereign AI Infrastructure With NVIDIA NVLink Fusion: NVIDIA Newsroom**
NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom announced a collaboration to advance Korea's sovereign AI infrastructure, supported by the Ministry of Science and ICT. NVLink Fusion is the link that brings together NVIDIA's open infrastructure platform, Rebellions' Korean-designed AI processors, and SK Telecom's AI data center, model and service capabilities. The same collaboration lays the groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to explore participation in the NVLink Fusion ecosystem. Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-rebellions-and-sk-telecom-announce-collaboration-to-advance-sovereign-ai-infrastructure-with-nvidia-nvlink-fusion) Source: [blogs.nvidia.com](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/korea-sovereign-ai-collaboration/)

**NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum: NVIDIA Blog**
At the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX, vice minister Ryu Je-myung and NVIDIA leaders met more than 20 Korean startups, and NVIDIA announced an investment in Point2 Technology. Point2 builds radio-frequency interconnects that move data between chips and racks in AI factories, offered as an alternative to copper and optical links for cluster scale-up. Additional investments are planned in Motif Technologies, RLWRLD and Upstage, and NVIDIA cited more than 1,000 Korea-based members of NVIDIA Inception. Source: [blogs.nvidia.com](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/korean-startup-investments-msit/)

**ASRock Rack Shows Early Xeon 7 Diamond Rapids Motherboard for Up to 4 TB of DDR5: TechPowerUp**
ASRock Rack's DMRD16-2L+, shown at the OCP Global Summit 2026 and detailed by ServeTheHome, reaches a theoretical bandwidth of roughly 1.6 TB/s and 4 TB of capacity when all 16 slots hold 256 GB MRDIMMs at up to 12,800 MT/s. Regular RDIMMs on the one-DIMM-per-channel, 16-channel layout top out at 128 GB and 8,000 MT/s. The 12-by-13-inch EEB board has no standard PCIe slots and no OCP NIC 3.0 connector; all I/O goes through up to 16 MCIO x8 connectors, each rated for PCIe 6.0 or CXL 3.0, for 128 lanes, plus one PCIe 5.0 x4 M.2 slot, two Intel I350 Gigabit Ethernet ports, an ASPEED AST2700 BMC with a dedicated management port, and VGA. Intel has the Xeon 7 family slated for a 2027 debut on the LGA9324 socket; the board is aimed at servers, and TechPowerUp says anyone planning a high-memory workstation for local AI will probably keep an eye on it. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354595/asrock-rack-shows-early-xeon-7-diamond-rapids-motherboard-for-up-to-4-tb-of-ddr5)

**Dell PowerEdge R770AP Review One Fast Intel Xeon 6 Server: ServeTheHome**
ServeTheHome reviewed Dell's PowerEdge R770AP, a 2U server built around a dual-socket Xeon 6 setup and 24 channels of DDR5. Source: [servethehome.com](https://www.servethehome.com/dell-poweredge-r770ap-review-one-fast-intel-xeon-6-server/)

### Data Centres & Power
**Every virtual megawatt needs a meter: Utility Dive**
Grid-enhancing technologies, demand response and virtual power plants all rely on the meter, a device utilities are about to replace by the millions. Source: [utilitydive.com](https://www.utilitydive.com/spons/every-virtual-megawatt-needs-a-meter/873408/)

**Building AI Kill Switches in Data Centers: Data Center Knowledge**
A data-center-level kill switch would shut down or isolate AI workloads facility by facility, cutting power, connectivity, or both, without fine-grained control of individual agents or models, and without necessarily stopping every process at once. Cutting the utility feed is unlikely to halt GPU servers, because UPS units and backup generators are built to ride through a grid outage and do not distinguish that outage from an intentional kill; abrupt power loss also risks the hardware, which is why operators resist it. Severing the network can stop external communication while workloads keep running inside the hall, but most modern facilities have multiple upstream carriers, redundant paths and diverse interconnection points, so every external path has to go dark. A single-site cut does not stop a model spread across facilities, and it does nothing once copies have already replicated outside; early detection is what makes the switch useful. Operators are unlikely to volunteer the capability, because the business is uptime, and a regulatory requirement aimed at network disconnection rather than power interruption only works if jurisdictions align — otherwise high-risk workloads move to facilities elsewhere. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/ai-data-centers/building-ai-kill-switches-in-data-centers)

**Hundreds arrested after Microsoft data center protest turns violent: Tom's Hardware**
A Microsoft data-center site is under construction, and Dutch police arrested 150 to 200 protesters after the action at that construction site turned violent. It is unclear which group entered the site first. The Stop Dirty Data Centers coalition demands a halt to AI data-center expansion, and police seized break-in tools and suspected stolen items from the construction site. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/hundreds-arrested-after-microsoft-data-center-protest-turns-violent-stop-dirty-data-centers-coalition-demands-halt-to-ai-data-center-expansion-dutch-police-seize-break-in-tools-suspected-stolen-items-from-construction-site)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**BofA: Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix Near a 'TSMC Moment' — Earnings Durability Is the Key to Re-rating: BigGo Finance**
Simon Woo of Bank of America, speaking on November 9, put South Korean memory makers' capital expenditure this year well above 100 trillion won, about $74.1 billion, against combined Chinese memory investment estimated at 20 trillion to 30 trillion won, about $14.8 billion to $22.2 billion, and he pointed to equipment import restrictions that apply only to Chinese companies. At Yangtze Memory, Chinese-made tools are about 20% of equipment at Wuhan fabs 1 and 2, a share expected to rise above 50% at new fab 3, with a plan under discussion to take fab 4 to at least 60% and as much as 70%. Fab 4 is expected to produce NAND with more than 300 stacked memory cells for AI data-center storage. Combined capacity at fabs 1 and 2 is around 200,000 wafers per month, and bringing fab 3 online would lift total capacity by about 25%. Counterpoint Research says YMTC held 14% of global NAND shipments in the second quarter of 2026, overtaking Kioxia for third place, eight percentage points behind SK Hynix at 22%, while a 33 billion yuan, about $4.9 billion, IPO by parent CCSH is temporarily suspended. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, through Solidigm, each run major NAND bases in Xi'an and Dalian, exposing them to U.S. equipment restrictions on China; the prevailing industry view in the piece is that more Chinese tools will not immediately close the technology gap, because high-layer NAND needs precision and stable yields, and enterprise SSD sales turn on reliability and customer relationships. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/a1ff1e4c-e5f7-4e1a-a9c6-ef27a006b7d1)

**Two Chinese companies cleared to buy banned Nvidia AI chips have empty offices and unknown addresses: Tom's Hardware**
New Matrix and Maginfra, both approved to receive H200 chips, appear to have abandoned offices and unknown addresses, and people in the buildings say they are unfamiliar with the companies or have never seen anyone working there. The investigation says the businesses have ties to sanctioned Chinese military suppliers. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/two-chinese-companies-cleared-to-buy-banned-nvidia-ai-chips-have-empty-offices-and-unknown-addresses-investigation-reveals-businesses-have-ties-to-sanctioned-chinese-military-suppliers)

### The Teardown: The Capacitor in the Wiring
A one-transistor, one-capacitor cell can sit in the metal stack above a processor instead of taking a die of its own. BigGo Finance describes that cell as back-end-of-line memory: the capacitor and its access transistor are built in the interconnect layers, not in the silicon where the logic transistors are drawn. The channel is an amorphous oxide semiconductor, deposited cold enough that the copper wiring underneath is not put through a process above 400 degrees Celsius. Conventional silicon transistors leak when they are off. The oxide channel's off-current is low enough, in the account BigGo Finance carries from the foundry's own presentation, to wipe out gate-induced drain leakage, which is what lets a capacitor hold charge without a six-transistor latch watching it.

That six-transistor latch is the SRAM bit cell. Six devices per bit is why cache eats area that could have been arithmetic. A capacitor cell uses one transistor and one capacitor. Spread across the wiring above a large processor, the same footprint holds more bits because the memory is no longer competing for the transistor layer. It is also not monolithic 3D DRAM in the usual sense, where memory cells are stacked vertically on a memory die. The array uses the fact that a processor die is typically much larger than a memory die, so the bits can spread out instead of climbing.

The test chip BigGo Finance cites, presented at the 2025 Symposium on VLSI Technology and Circuits, combines memory and logic on a single die and ran at 0.75 volts. It retained data beyond 128 milliseconds, finished random read and write cycles in under 8 nanoseconds, and withstood more than 10^14 program-and-erase cycles. Walk those in order. At 0.75 volts the array sits on a low logic-like rail, so the reported test did not need a separate high-voltage domain just to store a bit. Retention beyond 128 milliseconds means the cell held data for longer than a tenth of a second in that test; a designer still refreshes, but the leakage that forced SRAM's six transistors is the thing the oxide channel is there to cut. Under 8 nanoseconds is the random-cycle time the test chip showed, an access time, not a bandwidth for a stack of DRAM dies. More than 10^14 program-and-erase cycles is the endurance the presentation reported for that test chip.

Frederick Chen, quoted by BigGo Finance, puts the area argument in one comparison. Because the array can use the processor's larger footprint instead of a DRAM die's usually much smaller one, "It could be >10x," so the embedded array would not need as many layers as standalone monolithic 3D DRAM.

The same article records the foundry's public line. A spokesperson said TSMC focuses on its core business, dedicated IC foundry, and that its mission is "to be the trusted technology and capacity provider of the global logic IC industry for years to come." The statement never used the word DRAM. Chao Yu-chun, chair of Winbond Electronics, said a direct entry into conventional DRAM is unlikely, pointing to proprietary process technology and a tangled patent landscape, and noted that TSMC already works with memory makers including Samsung and Winbond on advanced packaging. An embedded layer, in the article's distinction, extends the foundry business. A full DRAM push would put the foundry in the merchant memory market beside Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.

This wiring-layer cell stops being the right substitute when the customer needs a merchant memory die with its own stack, sold beside the logic chip, rather than bits spread through the interconnect of a processor that is already large. If the logic die is not the bigger footprint Chen describes, the greater-than-ten-times area does not show up, and the layer count of a standalone 3D DRAM is back in the problem. An embedded capacitor also does not, on the figures reported, replace a high-bandwidth stack: the test chip's numbers are 0.75 volts, retention beyond 128 milliseconds, access under 8 nanoseconds, and endurance past 10^14 cycles, not a per-stack bandwidth. When the workload is that stack, the foundry's logic-capacity business and the memory makers' dies stay on opposite sides of the package. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/ffd14203-b248-4ceb-9974-5a6734bf97f3)

### On the Horizon
- TSMC's October sales update is due Tuesday at 1:30 p.m. Taipei time.
- Intel's Xeon 7 family is slated for a 2027 debut on the LGA9324 socket.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **120 megawatts went up in a year in Inner Mongolia, at a fifth of US cost.**

**What You Need to Know:** 120 megawatts went up in a year in Inner Mongolia, at a fifth of US cost. SemiAnalysis puts Galaxy, in Ulanqab, at up to 800 megawatts of IT capacity, with four phases built to suit two internet giants. The first phase is delivered; the rest of the campus was still a construction site on a September visit.

### Top Story
SemiAnalysis reports a September visit to Galaxy, a campus in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, planned for up to 800 megawatts of IT capacity, about the size of Stargate Abilene's core campus. The first 120-megawatt phase was delivered within a year at a fifth of US costs, and all four phases are built-to-suit for two internet giants. When the team visited, the rest of the campus was still a construction site. A local report put nearly 30,000 construction workers across 22 data-centre projects in the surrounding Chahar High-tech Zone. Envision Group owns the campus, has more than 100 gigawatts of wind turbines installed worldwide, builds its own wind farms and a dedicated power line to the site, and has a blade factory across the road. Source: [newsletter.semianalysis.com](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/we-visited-chinas-stargate-in-inner)

### Silicon
**TSMC Officially Denies DRAM Market Entry: Chosun**
Yesterday this show had TSMC studying paths into 3D DRAM. Chosun now reports that TSMC has officially denied a DRAM market entry. Source: [chosun.com](https://www.chosun.com/english/industry-en/2026/11/08/D7RE4QLHQBGJHDI44WHP3CLTGY/)

**ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+ Spotted with 16 DDR5 Slots for Diamond Rapids: ServeTheHome**
ServeTheHome has checked out the ASRock Rack DMRD16-2L+, a 16-channel Intel Diamond Rapids Xeon motherboard with 16 DDR5 slots and 128 PCIe Gen6 lanes over MCIO. Source: [servethehome.com](https://www.servethehome.com/asrock-rack-dmrd16-2l-plus-diamond-rapids-ocp-summit-2026/)

**Intel Razor Lake-S Reportedly Due in 2028 on LGA-1954: TechPowerUp**
Intel leaker Jaykihn says Razor Lake-S is not currently a 2027 product and is, for now, a 2028 product, on the LGA-1954 socket a leaked partner slide already ties to multiple generations after Nova Lake-S. That slide placed the first Nova Lake-S SKUs in the first quarter of 2027. Jaykihn describes new Griffin Cove performance cores as an entire tock, with the same core family also set for Coral Rapids Xeon while simultaneous multithreading stays exclusive to Xeon. Earlier leaks pointed to TSMC's N2X node for some Razor Lake production and to a 12-core Xe3P integrated GPU, originally meant for Nova Lake-S, moving to Razor Lake. HWiNFO has added Razor Lake-H, HX, and S in a recent beta. Intel has not confirmed the plan. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354565/intel-razor-lake-s-reportedly-due-in-2028-on-lga-1954)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Memory Suppliers May Set Q4 Revenue Records as HBM Prices Rise: TokenPost**
TokenPost reports that major memory suppliers may post record fourth-quarter revenue as new-generation HBM products roll out and prices rise. Samsung held 38 percent of the DRAM market in the third quarter. SK Hynix logged quarter-over-quarter revenue growth above 40 percent and regained part of its market share. Micron also grew on AI data-centre memory demand, at a pace that lagged Samsung and SK Hynix. The supplier named 长鑫存储 saw its market share climb to 9 percent, from 5 percent a year earlier. Source: [tokenpost.com](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/business/51217)

**CPU-Z Data Shows 16 GB RAM Gaining Ground While 32 GB and 64 GB RAM Shares Shrink: TechPowerUp**
CPU-Z developer Doc TB says validator statistics show PC RAM capacity declining year over year for the first time in that dataset, covering systems submitted over the last three months. Configurations of 32 GB are still the most common, at 37.2 percent, down 2.5 percent from a year ago, while 64 GB fell 18 percent to 7.3 percent. Shares moved the other way at 16 GB, up 12.9 percent to 33.0 percent, and at 8 GB, up 5.5 percent to 11.0 percent, while 96 GB and 128 GB setups each dropped by more than 26 percent. DDR4 is 54.5 percent of validations, up 6.0 percent, and DDR5 is 32.9 percent, down 2.9 percent. Steam's September survey had 32 GB ahead of 16 GB among gamers, and the October survey flipped that order. Team Group expects the worst of the shortage between the fourth quarter of 2026 and the second quarter of 2027, and DDR4 motherboards are expected for unannounced LGA1700 processors in early 2027. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354574/cpu-z-data-shows-16-gb-ram-gaining-ground-while-32-gb-and-64-gb-ram-shares-shrink)

### The Teardown: Ten Kilovolts, Then the Rack
A solid-state transformer takes medium-voltage alternating current and turns it into direct current for the rack in one box. In a 5-megawatt hall on the Galaxy campus, SemiAnalysis saw that box fed with 10-kilovolt alternating current and delivering 800-volt direct current. The stages it replaces are the ones a conventional hall stacks in a row: a low-voltage transformer, an uninterruptible power supply, and a rectifier. Each stage exists to change voltage or to clean it. Each stage also turns a slice of the incoming power into heat, and each one takes floor area, switchgear, and a maintenance window. Cutting them out shortens the path from the feeder to the server busbar and takes a whole electrical room out of the building programme.

Chinese data centres have been on some form of direct-current distribution for almost two decades, which is why an 800-volt solid-state step reads as a continuation rather than a first experiment. China Telecom ran 240-volt direct-current pilots in 2007. Alibaba's Panama power system came later on that same path. SemiAnalysis puts roughly a quarter of Chinese data centres built in the past decade on direct current, against about 97 percent of US data centres still on alternating-current uninterruptible supplies. The visitors note that this 800-volt architecture is still on the US roadmap, not in widespread American halls. An operator that already runs direct current at rack scale can treat the solid-state transformer as the next voltage step. An operator whose plant is still an AC UPS chain has to change the distribution practice, the protection scheme, and the spare-parts bench at the same time.

Walk the 5-megawatt hall as a power budget. Five megawatts of IT load has to cross from a 10-kilovolt feeder to an 800-volt bus. In the conventional chain that power would be stepped down, passed through or around a UPS, then rectified before it reached a rack power shelf. Three conversions, three sets of losses, three places a fault can open the path. The solid-state transformer does the voltage change and the AC-to-DC conversion together, so the hall's electrical plant is that transformer, the battery storage used to smooth the load, and the rack. The battery still matters because a wind-fed line does not hold a flat megawatt hour after hour. What disappears is the low-voltage transformer room and the UPS row that would otherwise sit between 10 kilovolts and the servers. Yield on that path is not a packaging yield. It is whether the medium-voltage gear holds its setpoint while the IT load swings, and whether a fault on one bus can be cleared without dropping the hall.

Cooling on the same campus uses one water loop for liquid-cooled and air-cooled servers, and it does so with no central chiller plant. That only works if the water the air-cooled gear can accept is water the climate can make. Nvidia has said Vera Rubin can run on 45-degree water without chillers. A US hall often keeps a chiller anyway, for air-cooled equipment and for the option to move load between the two cooling types. Galaxy drops the central plant and, SemiAnalysis writes, keeps much of that flexibility, in a design northern China has already run at scale. One loop means one water temperature for both kinds of server. The liquid-cooled machines can take warm water. The air-cooled machines set the ceiling, because their inlet has to stay inside what their fans and heat sinks can reject.

The shared loop fails its job the day air-cooled machines need inlet water colder than towers can make in that weather, because then either those machines run hot or a chiller has to pull the entire loop down. The 10-kilovolt solid-state step loses its reason when the utility handoff is already at low voltage, or when the site cannot maintain a medium-voltage direct-current bus with the practice that has been normal in Chinese halls since the 240-volt pilots of 2007. Source: [newsletter.semianalysis.com](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/we-visited-chinas-stargate-in-inner)

### On the Horizon
- Razor Lake-S is currently slated for 2028, and a leaked partner slide places the first Nova Lake-S SKUs in the first quarter of 2027.
- Team Group expects the worst of the memory shortage between the fourth quarter of 2026 and the second quarter of 2027.
- DDR4 motherboards for unannounced LGA1700 processors are expected in early 2027.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **TSMC is studying two paths into 3D DRAM Nvidia wants made in-house.**

**What You Need to Know:** TSMC is studying two paths into 3D DRAM after a request from Nvidia: build a new fab, or buy a plant and convert it. The Information’s November 6 report, carried by several outlets, describes cell-stacked memory, not an extension of the HBM4 base-die work TSMC already does with SK hynix. No investment decision has been made, and TSMC says its focus remains logic foundry.

### Top Story
The Information reported on November 6 that TSMC is considering manufacturing 3D DRAM, stacking memory cells vertically inside a die, and igor’sLAB says the push followed a request from Nvidia. Hsu Kuo-chin, a TSMC vice president in Advanced Packaging who previously worked at Micron in Taiwan, is said to be leading work on production concepts. The options described are a new fab or an acquired plant converted for memory; Seoul Economic Daily reports that no decision has been made on whether to invest, how much to spend, or when output would begin. TSMC told The Information it does not comment on market rumors and stays focused on logic foundry work, including the phrasing that it remains “focused on our core business at all times” and “the trusted technology and capacity provider” of logic chips. Nvidia did not reply, and Reuters could not independently verify the account. This is not the April 19, 2024 SK hynix collaboration, in which TSMC’s role is the HBM4 base die and CoWoS packaging, with HBM4 mass production planned for 2026 rather than recorded as a finished result. Cell-stacked 3D DRAM forms the cells in one die; HBM stacks finished DRAM dies. BigGo Finance, citing Counterpoint Research, puts global DRAM revenue in the third quarter of 2026 up 369 percent year on year, with Samsung at 38 percent, SK hynix at 29 percent, Micron at 21 percent, and CXMT at 9 percent, and cites TrendForce expecting conventional DRAM contract prices up another 10 to 15 percent quarter on quarter in the fourth quarter. TechPowerUp notes Micron has decided not to bring 4F² DRAM to market and is on a 3D DRAM path; BigGo cites Micron’s completed March purchase of Powerchip’s P5 fab in Tongluo, Miaoli, for 1.8 billion dollars, announced in January, as the kind of acquire-and-convert move now being discussed for TSMC. Source: [xenospectrum.com](https://xenospectrum.com/en/tsmc-3d-dram-hbm-boundary/) · [igorslab.de](https://www.igorslab.de/en/tsmc-3d-dram-nvidia-memory-chips/) · [en.sedaily.com](https://en.sedaily.com/finance/2026/11/07/tsmc-weighs-3d-dram-push-at-nvidias-request) · [briefs.co](https://www.briefs.co/news/tsmc-mulls-3d-dram-push-as-nvidia-seeks-more-ai-memory/) · [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/016d496b-fb93-48b7-8f9c-0b2e2fdcb8a2) · [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354547/tsmc-is-reportedly-considering-3d-dram-production) · [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/tsmc-considers-making-advanced-memory-chips-information-reports-2026-11-06/)

### Silicon
**Diamond Foundry Announces First-Ever D200mm Single-Crystal Diamond: Semiconductor Digest**
Diamond Foundry announced the first D200mm single-crystal diamond, 200 millimeters in diameter, and said the crystal is neither an assembly of pieces nor a polycrystalline wafer. Chief executive Martin Roscheisen called it “one of those milestones that once seemed almost impossible,” credited hundreds of engineers, and said the result “makes D300mm predictable as well.” Stefan Gsell and Martin Fischer have pursued scalable single-crystal diamond for 25 years. The announcement accompanied a video keynote by Roscheisen at CarbonSemi 2026 in Ningbo, and the first crystal is shown as grown and unpolished. The company points to diamond’s thermal conductivity as a way to spread heat from AI processors that concentrate power in small regions of silicon. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/diamond-foundry-announces-first-ever-d200mm-single-crystal-diamond/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=diamond-foundry-announces-first-ever-d200mm-single-crystal-diamond) · [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354540/diamond-foundry-announces-first-ever-d200mm-single-crystal-diamond)

**Hanyang University Researchers Gain Control Over Where Semiconductor Crystals First Form: Semiconductor Digest**
Hanyang University researchers report a method that controls where semiconductor crystals first form. The method guides single crystals to begin growing in predefined central regions. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/hanyang-university-researchers-gain-control-over-where-semiconductor-crystals-first-form/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=hanyang-university-researchers-gain-control-over-where-semiconductor-crystals-first-form)

**Can Optical AI Cut Data Center Inference Power Use?: Data Center Knowledge**
Lumai is testing optical AI servers in a UK lab. The test asks whether shifting inference prefill off GPUs can ease data-centre power constraints. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/ai-data-centers/can-optical-ai-cut-data-center-inference-power-use-)

### Data Centres & Power
**Duke Energy to stay course on data center-fueled growth plan after ‘historic’ election: Utility Dive**
Duke Energy’s large-load pipeline stands at 15.4 gigawatts and has stayed virtually unchanged since the first quarter of 2026. The company is staying on a 103 billion dollar spending plan heavily focused on new natural gas generation after the election. Source: [utilitydive.com](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/historic-election-night-wont-change-growth-focus-at-duke-energy-executi/873965/)

**SpaceXAI plans data center in Arizona, Musk's firm claims it will have 6GW capacity: Data Center Dynamics**
SpaceXAI’s Arizona data centre is announced, with the firm claiming 6 gigawatts of capacity. Construction work could start in March 2027. The project is a plan with a claimed capacity, not an energized site. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/spacexai-data-center-arizona-cochise-county-elon-musk/)

**ING Bank looks to sell $500m in data center loans at once, including at Stargate site: Data Center Dynamics**
ING Bank is looking to sell 500 million dollars of data-centre loans in one go, including loans at a Stargate site. Data Center Dynamics describes the sale as further unsettling investors in a shaky market. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/ing-bank-looks-to-sell-500m-in-data-center-loans-at-once-including-at-stargate-site/)

**AWS Targets Metadata-Intensive HPC Workloads with FSx for Lustre Intelligent-Tiering Update: HPCwire**
Amazon Web Services announced on November 6 that Amazon FSx for Lustre now supports up to 192,000 metadata I/O operations per second on file systems using the Intelligent-Tiering storage class. That ceiling is 16 times the previous maximum of 12,000 IOPS. The update is aimed at metadata-intensive high-performance computing workloads. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/aws-targets-metadata-intensive-hpc-workloads-with-fsx-for-lustre-intelligent-tiering-update/)

**Two days of anti-data center protests planned across Europe: Data Center Dynamics**
Stop Dirty Data Centres has planned two days of action across Europe, Data Center Dynamics reports, after anti-data-centre results in the US midterms. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/two-days-of-anti-data-center-protest-planned-across-europe/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Six Pallets of NVIDIA Hardware Worth $11.4 Million Stolen on the Way to Texas: TechPowerUp**
Oakland police are investigating the theft of six pallets of Nvidia hardware worth 11.4 million dollars that were bound for Fort Worth, Texas. A truck carrying a food-transport company’s logo picked up the cargo in Oakland on August 29 and then went off the grid heading south, with several multi-hour stops before police lost track of it in San Bernardino County. The loss was noticed in early September and reported to Oakland police on September 13. UC Berkeley professor Olaf Groth told ABC7 that Nvidia chips can sell for roughly double their US price abroad, with a 550,000 dollar compute system going for 1 million dollars or more, and that the heists are getting bigger and more complex. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354551/six-pallets-of-nvidia-hardware-worth-usd-11-4-million-stolen-on-the-way-to-texas)

**Eulitha Ramps Up Deliveries of Advanced Lithography Systems: Semiconductor Digest**
Eulitha announced deliveries of multiple automated lithography tools to foundries. The tools are for production of indium phosphide distributed-feedback lasers used in AI data centres. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/eulitha-ramps-up-deliveries-of-advanced-lithography-systems/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=eulitha-ramps-up-deliveries-of-advanced-lithography-systems)

### Also Today
**Nvidia Said to Finance SPIL’s CoWoS Expansion With Billions: FourWeekMBA**
Nvidia is said to be financing an expansion of SPIL’s CoWoS capacity, with the reported sum described as billions. Source: [fourweekmba.com](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-nvidia-said-to-finance-spils-cowos-expansion-with-billions/)

**AI Chip Boom Triggers $28 Billion Race to Expand Advanced Packaging Capacity: Tekedia**
Tekedia describes an AI chip boom that has triggered a 28 billion dollar race to expand advanced packaging capacity. Source: [tekedia.com](https://www.tekedia.com/ai-chip-boom-triggers-28-billion-race-to-expand-advanced-packaging-capacity/)

**Paras Defence Teams With BroadPak For Semiconductor Packaging Push: Rediff**
Paras Defence has teamed with BroadPak for a semiconductor packaging push. Source: [rediff.com](https://www.rediff.com/business/report/paras-semiconductors-broadpak-partner-for-advanced-packaging/20261106.htm)

**Baseten Prepay Requirements in Compute Market: Dylan Patel**
Dylan Patel says Baseten has to make massive prepays in the current compute market, in the same way others put money into capex. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/dylan522p/status/2118809629706928176)

### The Teardown: When Attention Is Sixty Percent of the Step
On a single Nvidia B200, the NVIDIA Technical Blog puts attention at about 60 percent of diffusion-transformer GPU kernel time for FLUX 3 Image Klein at 2048 by 2048 under NVFP4, with vanilla BF16 attention, for both the Base checkpoint and the distilled one. Generating the image is a loop. A text encoder, here Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct, conditions the job. A diffusion transformer then refines a noisy latent, step after step, and an autoencoder turns the latent into pixels, or encodes a reference image when the job is an edit. The loop, not the final decode, is where the clock goes. Higher resolution makes the attention matrices larger, so the same step count costs more. Blackwell’s NVFP4 format cuts the weight and activation traffic of the matrix multiplies that feed that attention. TensorRT LLM VisualGen then fuses those multiplies with their epilogues, including SwiGLU and the query-key-value projections that also apply normalization and rotary embeddings, through FlashInfer PrimsTS kernels.

The blog’s own ladder shows how the gains stack, and where they stop stacking cleanly. Against uncompiled BF16 on one B200 at 2048 by 2048, the combined optimizations reach up to 3.46 times faster text-to-image and 4.45 times faster image-to-image for the Base model. NVFP4 alone, before those extra layers, is up to 1.62 times faster text-to-image and 1.58 times faster image-to-image than BF16. The latency table that follows uses NVFP4, vanilla attention, and torch.compile, averaged over 10 requests after two warmup requests. Base runs 50 denoising steps with a classifier-free guidance scale of 3.5, which means a guided pass and an unguided pass. The distilled Klein runs 16 steps and drops guidance. That is why a format win and a step-count win are different levers: one shrinks each pass, the other deletes passes. Pinned NVFP4 PrimsTS kernels add only 1.02 to 1.10 times on text-to-image versus the autotuned TensorRT LLM NVFP4 GEMM, so kernel fusion is a small slice once the format is already NVFP4. Quantized attention is larger. VC-Attention FP8 with a repair budget of 0.005 reaches 1.18 times on both Base and distilled at 2048 by 2048, with LPIPS of 0.086 on Base and 0.151 on distilled. Sol-Attention at tau of 1.0 with 12 initial dense steps gives 1.30 times faster denoising plus decoding on Base; holding 16 dense steps for fidelity drops that to 1.24 times. Cache-DiT step caching nearly halves Base latency at both 1024 by 1024 and 2048 by 2048, and reaches 1.94 times at the higher resolution with an LPIPS of 0.033. Across eight B200 GPUs, classifier-free guidance parallelism and Ulysses parallelism cut median text-to-image latency from 14.90 seconds to 3.00 seconds on Base and from 2.73 seconds to 1.08 seconds on distilled, with denoising speedups of 6.01 times and 4.44 times. The model itself was trained on a GB200 NVL72.

The 12-step Sol-Attention schedule stops being the right schedule when the job needs the 16 dense steps that pull Base’s denoising-plus-decode gain from 1.30 times down to 1.24 times, or when an LPIPS of 0.151 on the distilled checkpoint, under the same 1.18 times VC-Attention setting that scores 0.086 on Base, is already past what the edit can accept. Source: [developer.nvidia.com](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/speed-up-image-generation-with-flux-3-image-klein-on-nvidia-blackwell-gpus/)

### On the Horizon
- Construction work on the announced SpaceXAI Arizona plan could start in March 2027.
- Cosmic Group is scheduled at SEMICON Europa 2026 in Munich, booth C1255, from November 10 to November 13, held with electronica.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Reported China orders of six million RTX PRO 5500s exceed a reported three-million 2027 build.**

**What You Need to Know:** Reported orders from China for Nvidia’s RTX PRO 5500 top six million cards, against a source’s ceiling of three million units that can be built in 2027, while a US listing prices the cut-down card above the flagship RTX PRO 6000. Reuters, via Semiconductor Engineering, puts about 600,000 H200 chips in Hong Kong awaiting approval for mainland shipment as Beijing limits imports. A European Commission analysis puts EU fab production costs 40% to 50% above Taiwan, South Korea, and China, and US voters moved to kill or slow data-center projects near them.

### Top Story
Chinese buyers have ordered Nvidia’s RTX PRO 5500 past a reported 2027 build ceiling, and a US government reseller lists the cut-down card above the flagship. TechPowerUp reports that SHI Government Solutions listed a PNY-built RTX PRO 5500 at an MSRP of $17,999 and a discounted $17,408.63, while Nvidia’s own US marketplace lists the RTX PRO 6000 at $16,000 even though that card has 24,064 CUDA cores and 96 GB of memory against the 5500’s 21,760 cores and 84 GB. At the discounted listing the lesser card is still around $1,400 more, and Nvidia has not posted an official price since quietly adding the 5500 in September, so TechPowerUp says it is unclear whether $17,999 is Nvidia’s figure or PNY’s. Videocardz, citing Reuters, reports that ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent have ordered more than 3 million cards at roughly $11,400 each, with total orders from China reportedly topping 6 million, while one source said Nvidia can make no more than 3 million of them in 2027. With the B300 barred from China and the H200 reviewed case by case, TechPowerUp calls the 5500 one of the strongest Nvidia GPUs Chinese firms can still buy; the card carries 28 GDDR7 modules, and the outlet says orders ahead of supply are a reason to expect the price to stay high. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354527/nvidia-rtx-pro-5500-listing-spotted-at-usd-17-999-more-than-the-flagship-rtx-pro-6000)

### Silicon
**Skymizer and MiTAC to Showcase Single-Server Kimi K3 Platform at SC26: HPCwire**
Skymizer and MiTAC have announced a joint SC26 showcase aimed at running Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, on one MiTAC server. The box they describe carries eight Skymizer HTX301 LPU cards and 2 TB of card-attached memory. This is a showcase target, not a stated deployment: the companies say they aim to run that model on the single server. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/skymizer-and-mitac-to-showcase-single-server-kimi-k3-platform-at-sc26/)

**Supermicro Launches KV Cache Solution with IBM and NVIDIA: HPCwire**
Supermicro on November 5 announced a KV-cache storage solution with IBM and Nvidia for inference. It pairs Supermicro Petascale all-flash storage servers using AMD EPYC 9005 Series processors, Turin, with IBM Storage Scale, the Nvidia Dynamo inference framework, and Spectrum-X Ethernet. The announcement is of the joint stack, not of a named site turning it on. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/supermicro-launches-kv-cache-solution-with-ibm-and-nvidia/)

**Intel Core Ultra 4000 Series "Nova Lake-H" SoC Surfaces: TechPowerUp**
A reported die photo adds a measured package map for the Core Ultra 4000 Nova Lake-H part already tied to Intel’s 18A-P process. TechPowerUp describes a 4+8+4 configuration — 4 P-cores, 8 E-cores, and 4 LPE-cores — on a compute die made on Intel 18A-P, in a package of about 12 by 23 mm and 276 mm². The graphics tile, on Intel 3-E, holds 4 Xe GPU cores in roughly 26 mm², beside a 21 mm² dummy die; a 72 mm² 18A-P die hosts the 4 LPE-cores as a central hub, a peripheral control tile measures 58 mm², and the 4P+8E compute tile measures 55 mm², both on 18A-P. The outlet presents this as a raw picture that surfaced, not as an Intel launch. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354506/intel-core-ultra-4000-series-nova-lake-h-soc-surfaces)

**AMD "Medusa Point" With 10-Core, 20-Thread CPU Configuration Surfaces: TechPowerUp**
An AMD Medusa Point sample has surfaced on Geekbench as a 10-core, 20-thread part split into 4 Zen 6 cores and 6 Zen 6c cores, not as a formal launch. Each core shows 32 KB of L1 instruction cache, 48 KB of L1 data cache, and 1 MB of L2, with a shared 16 MB L3; the listing gives a 2.0 GHz base and a maximum of 1996 MHz, which TechPowerUp treats as a misread of early silicon. The instruction set on the sample includes AVX-512, AVX512-FP16, and AVX512-VNNI, and the test system had 64 GB of DDR5, 55.58 GB usable, at 5,188 MT/s. Talk of an RDNA 4m mobile graphics block remains rumor in the same report; what the listing measured is the CPU configuration and those instruction extensions. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354504/amd-medusa-point-with-10-core-20-thread-cpu-configuration-surfaces)

### Data Centres & Power
**Google to serve as credit backstop for TeraWulf data center in Kentucky: Data Center Dynamics**
Google is to serve as credit backstop for a TeraWulf data center in Kentucky that is contracted to Anthropic under a $19 billion deal. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/google-to-serve-as-credit-backstop-for-terawulf-data-center-in-kentucky/)

**Bank of England queries speculative data center loans tied to projects without tenants: Data Center Dynamics**
The Bank of England is querying speculative data-center loans tied to projects without tenants, trying to understand the scale of risk in the sector. The report is of the inquiry, not of a published exposure total. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/bank-of-england-queries-speculative-data-center-loans-tied-to-projects-without-tenants/)

**Eaton CEO: AC to DC migration for data centers is real: Utility Dive**
Eaton chief executive Paulo Ruiz says the migration from AC to DC for data centers “is real,” and that Eaton is investing in solid-state transformers to meet it. He also said the “timing of that transition is not under our control.” Source: [utilitydive.com](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/eaton-ceo-ac-to-dc-migration-is-real-because-of-large-power-savings/873887/)

**Anti-Data Center Sentiment Rides Blue Wave, Threatening AI Boom: HPCwire**
HPCwire reports that this week’s US election, a major Democratic victory, came with voters moving to kill or slow data-center projects near them. The outlet says that souring local sentiment called the longevity of the current AI buildout into question and punished tech stocks. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/2026/11/05/anti-data-center-sentiment-rides-blue-wave-threatening-ai-boom/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Nvidia H200s held in Hong Kong: Semiconductor Engineering**
Reuters, via Semiconductor Engineering, reports that approximately 600,000 Nvidia H200 AI chips are being held in Hong Kong awaiting approval for shipment to mainland China. Beijing has limited imports in an effort to reduce reliance on US technology and encourage adoption of domestically developed processors. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/chip-industry-week-in-review-163/)

**Europe’s Chip Industry: Perfect Storm or Perfect Timing?: EE Times**
SEMICON Europa 2026, co-located with electronica in Munich from November 10 to 13, is framed as “Europe’s Next Era: Navigating the Perfect Storm.” A European Commission analysis published in June 2026 finds total fab production costs in EU fabs 40% to 50% higher than in Taiwan, South Korea, and China; in 2024 the EU consumed €55 billion of semiconductors and imported €43.6 billion from outside the bloc, with the sharpest exposure in leading-edge chips for AI and high-performance computing. The European Court of Auditors concluded in 2025 that the first Chips Act strategy is very unlikely to deliver a 20% EU share of global market value by 2030, and the share is now projected at 11.7% by 2030. Chips Act 2.0, published in June 2026 and targeted for adoption in the second quarter of 2027, keeps advanced manufacturing but widens the frame to design, equipment, materials, and advanced packaging, pilot lines, and customers in automotive, industrial systems, and data centers. SEMI Europe president Laith Altimime said, “Europe’s semiconductor competitiveness depends on the strength of the entire ecosystem, from design and materials to equipment, manufacturing, and advanced packaging.” Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/europe-chip-industry-perfect-storm-or-perfect-timing/)

Micron has not confirmed the suspension. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/chip-industry-week-in-review-163/)

### Also Today
**India targets creating homegrown GPUs within 2 years and plans to commercialize indigenous SHAKTI and VEGA processors: Tom's Hardware**
MeitY secretary S. Krishnan says India plans a homegrown GPU under Semiconductor Mission 2.0 in about two years and intends to commercialize its SHAKTI and VEGA RISC-V processors while expanding domestic server production. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/india-targets-creating-homegrown-gpus-within-2-years-and-plans-to-commercialize-indigenous-shakti-and-vega-risc-v-processors-sees-ai-boom-as-a-potential-repeat-of-the-y2k-opportunity-for-its-it-industry)

Entegris expanded its partnership with Kioxia to accelerate materials work for future generations of BiCS Flash 3D flash memory. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/entegris-expands-partnership-with-kioxia/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=entegris-expands-partnership-with-kioxia)

**Macronix’s sNOVA Technology Recognized with IEEE Milestone Award: Semiconductor Digest**
Macronix’s sNOVA industrial production-optimization platform received an IEEE Milestone Award, the first for a semiconductor company in Taiwan. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/macronixs-snova-technology-recognized-with-ieee-milestone-award/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=macronixs-snova-technology-recognized-with-ieee-milestone-award)

Chemours released two fluids for two-phase liquid cooling, aimed at direct-to-chip and immersion. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/chemours-releases-two-fluids-for-two-phase-liquid-cooling/)

**Moonshot AI Looks to Europe to Lease Nvidia Blackwell Clusters, Report Says: BigGo Finance**
Moonshot AI is reported to be looking to Europe to lease Nvidia Blackwell clusters. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/fb73515c-f8fc-4bc2-8296-366fc0714820)

**MediaTek Recruits Intel Packaging Veteran Navid Shahriari as AI Chip Push Accelerates: BigGo Finance**
MediaTek has recruited Intel packaging veteran Navid Shahriari as its AI chip push accelerates. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/fb54a87a-9851-41f5-8d0d-b75b61833c57)

**Taiwan's reported 1nm chip site plan in Tainan: NeoTeo**
NeoTeo reports a Taiwan plan for a 1 nm chipmaking site in Tainan. Source: [neoteo.com](https://www.neoteo.com/en/taiwan-reportedly-plans-a-tainan-site-for-1nm-chipmaking)

**Arista Lines Up Networking For 10 Gigawatts Of AI Systems: The Next Platform**
The Next Platform reports that Arista is lining up networking for 10 gigawatts of AI systems. Source: [nextplatform.com](https://www.nextplatform.com/connect/2026/11/05/arista-lines-up-networking-for-10-gigawatts-of-ai-systems/5307929)

### The Teardown: The Decoder Beside the Qubit
Error correction is a split job. The quantum chip holds a fragile state; a classical machine has to decide, continuously, which error just happened and which fix to apply before that state drifts. HPCwire’s account of the November 5, 2026 announcement from IBM, the Quantum Science Center at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, and AMD describes a bench built for that split. IBM’s piece is the Nighthawk processor: 120 qubits, square-lattice connectivity, a high rate of circuits per second, and pulse control that can act while a circuit is still running. Oak Ridge’s piece is Umbra, powered by AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs and 5th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs. They are co-located so a team can score each error-correction method by qubits, time, samples, and classical cost.

On that quantum hardware a researcher can measure qubits mid-calculation and branch on the result immediately, set the timing of the pulses that guard the qubits, see what the machine actually ran, and work from the raw measurement signal. A code uses many noisy physical qubits to stand in for fewer logical qubits a scientist can trust. The classical decoder reads the syndrome — the pattern of those stabilizer checks — and names the correction. If the name arrives late, it refers to a state that has already moved. Umbra is there so that decoder can be tried on GPU nodes large enough to resemble the classical side a later machine would need, and so competing codes can be ranked by the classical burden they impose. The announcement is explicit that the open question is no longer whether error correction can work on quantum hardware, but how to accelerate and optimize it.

The figures in the HPCwire account separate a modest qubit step from a large operations step. IBM’s recorded experiments have reached up to 70 logical qubits and 438 hard operations. The Department of Energy’s Quantum Genesis mission, through its Q Competition, targets 100 logical qubits running 100,000 hard operations by late 2028. From 70 logical qubits to 100 is 30 more logical qubits, under half again the demonstrated count. From 438 hard operations to 100,000 is the gap the announcement calls roughly 230-fold. Closing that gap, the write-up says, is what the field still has to do. A decoder that keeps up for a few hundred operations has not shown it can keep up when each added operation is another round of measurement and another classical decision. Stretch the circuit by that roughly 230-fold factor and a decoder that was merely fast enough beside Nighthawk becomes the limit, even though the logical-qubit count only had to rise by 30.

This first pairing stops being the right instrument the day the code needs a 121st physical qubit, because 120 is all Nighthawk brings, or the day the question is 100,000 hard operations rather than 438. The announcement says next approaches need those pulse-level controls together on systems large enough to test real codes, and it lists the stack that has to arrive as one piece: concatenated codes, space-time codes, algorithm-aware decoders, hardware-aware compilation, and software orchestration. Until a larger quantum processor shares the bench, Umbra’s job is to price methods in qubits, time, samples, and classical resources, not to deliver the late-2028 operation count. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/ornl-ibm-and-amd-launch-new-co-design-platform-for-quantum-error-correction/)

- Second quarter of 2027: targeted adoption of the European Commission’s Chips Act 2.0 proposal.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Nvidia ships CUDA 13.5, taking Vera Rubin from early access into production deployments.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nvidia has shipped CUDA 13.5, moving Vera Rubin into production on a platform it has described as up to 144 GPUs per rack. Samsung’s second Taylor, Texas fab is reported fully booked, mostly by AMD, for 2 nm HBM base dies. SEMI counted 3,756 million square inches of silicon wafers shipped in the third quarter.

### Top Story
Nvidia on Wednesday shipped CUDA Toolkit 13.5, moving the Vera Rubin platform from early developer access to general availability for enterprise production, and shipped it with Linux driver 620.70.06. The platform pairs Rubin GPUs with Vera CPUs over NVLink-C2C. Nvidia said in June 2026 that Vera Rubin systems would pack up to 144 GPUs per rack and deliver more than 7 exaflops of AI-for-science throughput and 5 petaflops of native FP64. CUDA 13.5 adds tuned matrix-multiplication heuristics and kernel adjustments for the platform’s NVFP4 and MXFP8 operations, which Nvidia says lift throughput without per-shape autotuning. Rubin and later GPUs support the Windows Display Driver Model and Microsoft Compute Driver Model but no longer support Tesla Compute Cluster mode, so applications and deployment scripts built around TCC need reworking. The release also extends Windows on Arm support to DGX Station for Windows, and it adds Multi-Process Service v3 weighted timeslicing plus locality-domain controls that let an application choose uniform streaming-multiprocessor partitions or partitions that draw on every available SM. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/ce0054f3-0d38-4ea1-81c5-6016102ce678) · [developer.nvidia.com](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-cuda-13-5-brings-nvidia-vera-rubin-ga-support/)

### Silicon
**Samsung's 2 nm Taylor Fab 2 Reportedly Fully Booked, Mostly by AMD: TechPowerUp**
Korea’s Maeil Business Newspaper, citing industry sources, reports that Samsung has booked the entire planned output of Taylor Fab 2 in Texas, with most of it going to AMD. The fab will make HBM base dies for AMD and NVIDIA on a 2 nm process, and AMD’s volume alone is described as enough to stretch the fab’s capacity. Samsung declined to comment, saying it cannot confirm customer-related details. The base die is the logic chip at the bottom of an HBM stack; Samsung plans to pair the Texas-made dies with DRAM produced in South Korea and ship finished HBM. Current HBM4 and sampled HBM4E use 4 nm base dies, so 2 nm or smaller is aimed at later HBM generations. The report follows Lisa Su’s October visit to Samsung, when Samsung reportedly wanted foundry orders from AMD in return for HBM AMD needs, and a March memorandum that made Samsung the primary HBM4 supplier for the Instinct MI455X. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354477/samsungs-2-nm-taylor-fab-2-reportedly-fully-booked-mostly-by-amd)

**Arm Delivers a Record Second Quarter, Reaching $1.44B in Total Revenue: TechPowerUp**
Arm, in a shareholder letter published November 4, 2026, reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Total revenue rose 27 percent year over year to $1.44 billion, which Arm called its highest-ever second quarter. Licensing and other revenue was $773 million, up 50 percent year over year, and royalty revenue was $670 million, with data-center royalties doubling year over year. Partners reported more than 10 billion Arm-based chips shipped in the quarter, an increase of 1.5 billion chips year over year, on a platform Arm says is already used by more than 30 million developers. Arm’s own note on the quarter said both its IP business and its new silicon business are showing rapid growth on the same compute platform. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354485/arm-delivers-a-record-second-quarter-reaching-usd-1-44b-in-total-revenue)

**AMD Guidance Points to Its First Quarter Ever With More Revenue Than Intel: TechPowerUp**
AMD guided fourth-quarter revenue to approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3 percent, or roughly $16.5 billion to $17.5 billion, while Intel expects $15 billion to $16 billion. The bottom of AMD’s range sits above the top of Intel’s, so the crossover holds unless either company misses guidance badly. AMD’s Data Center segment hit a record $8.5 billion in the third quarter, up 97 percent year over year, on EPYC demand and the launch of Instinct MI450 Series GPUs inside Helios racks. AMD expects that segment to grow about 50 percent sequentially in the fourth quarter, while Client and Gaming is expected to drop by more than 20 percent. Intel’s fourth-quarter outlook includes a two-week shutdown at Fab 28 in Israel that Intel says will cost about $300 million in fourth-quarter revenue. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354470/amd-guidance-points-to-its-first-quarter-ever-with-more-revenue-than-intel)

**Universal Quantum Launches iQPU Integrated Trapped-Ion Processor: HPCwire**
Universal Quantum on November 4, 2026 launched the iQPU, an integrated quantum processing unit meant to be manufactured, scaled, and deployed as a unit rather than a loose assembly of ion traps and control electronics. It combines a trapped-ion compute surface with built-in ultra-low-noise control and modular chip-to-chip interconnects the company calls UQConnect. The launch was announced from Haywards Heath, England, and Hamburg, Germany. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/universal-quantum-launches-iqpu-integrated-trapped-ion-processor/)

### Data Centres & Power
**Modular AI Data Centers Gain Ground as Crusoe Debuts Unit: Data Center Knowledge**
Crusoe has debuted the Spark Liquid, a factory-built modular data-center unit rated at 3.5 megawatts, as a faster path to AI capacity than a conventional hall. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/modular-data-centers/modular-ai-data-centers-gain-ground-as-crusoe-debuts-unit)

**APS expects sales to double by 2041, plans extending coal use to 2038: Utility Dive**
Arizona Public Service, in an integrated resource plan filed Friday with regulators, expects sales to double by 2041 and peak demand to grow about 3.4 percent a year over the next 15 years, driven by industry and data centers. The plan proposes extending coal use to 2038. Source: [utilitydive.com](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/aps-sales-double-by-2041-proposes-extending-coal-use-to-2038/873648/)

**atNorth signs deal with Calentix for heat reuse at SWE04 data center in Sollefteå, Sweden: Data Center Dynamics**
atNorth has signed a deal with Calentix to reuse heat from the SWE04 data center in Sollefteå, Sweden, with the first delivery of heat expected in 2029. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/atnorth-signs-deal-with-calentix-for-heat-reuse-at-swe04-data-center-in-sollefte%C3%A5-sweden/)

**Local data center moratoria, limits, and restrictions voted in across the US: Data Center Dynamics**
Local data-center moratoria, limits, and restrictions were voted in across the United States, and most of the anti-data-center measures passed, with Ohio leading the charge. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/local-data-center-moratoria-limits-and-restrictions-voted-in-across-the-us/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Nvidia tells data center partners to cut China exposure, limits RTX chip sales to mainland: Data Center Dynamics**
Nvidia has told data-center partners to cut China exposure and is limiting RTX chip sales to mainland China, as the United States and China both move to decouple. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/nvidia-tells-data-center-partners-to-cut-china-exposure-limits-rtx-chip-sales-to-mainland/)

**TSMC stock in focus as Tesla reopens Texas Terafab talks: ad-hoc-news.de**
A November 2 report by El Fondo, citing supply-chain sources and a DigiTimes account, said Elon Musk had softened his earlier position and that talks could reopen toward TSMC taking primary responsibility for building and operating Tesla’s planned Terafab in Texas. Tesla and SpaceX had previously been described as planning to build and run the plant themselves, with TSMC potentially limited to subleasing part of the site. Equity ownership and investment arrangements are still under negotiation, and Tesla, SpaceX, and TSMC had not immediately commented. Intel was previously linked after Musk said Tesla planned to use Intel’s next-generation 14A process; the latest report did not clarify whether that role would change. On SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call, Musk said he aimed to have a test chip operating around May or June 2027 at an Austin research fab, and described volume production at Terafab in the third or fourth quarter of 2028 as an aspiration. Source: [ad-hoc-news.de](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/tsmc-stock-in-focus-as-tesla-reopens-texas-terafab-talks/70462128)

**Nintendo ROM chip supplier Macronix quits to focus on chips for AI data centers, reports indicate: Tom's Hardware**
Macronix, one of Nintendo’s ROM chip manufacturers, is shutting down that business to reallocate manufacturing to NOR and NAND flash chips that the AI industry demands, according to reports. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/video-games/nintendo/nintendo-rom-chip-supplier-macronix-quits-to-focus-on-chips-for-ai-data-centers-game-key-cards-may-be-more-available-as-large-game-storage-chips-become-more-expensive)

**Worldwide Silicon Wafer Shipments Increase 13.4% Year-on-Year in Q3 2026, SEMI Reports: Semiconductor Digest**
SEMI’s Silicon Manufacturers Group reported worldwide silicon wafer shipments of 3,756 million square inches in the third quarter of 2026, up 13.4 percent from 3,313 million square inches in the same quarter of 2025 and up 5.1 percent from 3,573 million square inches in the second quarter of 2026. Masatsugu Miura, chairman of SEMI SMG and a SUMCO sales and marketing general manager, said the increase was supported by AI-related demand that has broadened beyond advanced logic and memory to power devices and photonics, plus stronger industrial demand from robotics, AI server power supplies, and general-purpose industrial semiconductors. Bonding and advanced packaging also continued to support demand for 300 mm polished wafers. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/worldwide-silicon-wafer-shipments-increase-13-4-year-on-year-in-q3-2026-semi-reports/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=worldwide-silicon-wafer-shipments-increase-13-4-year-on-year-in-q3-2026-semi-reports)

### Also Today
**Semiconductor Market Continues to Accelerate in Q3 2026: Semiconductor Digest**
The European Semiconductor Industry Association said global semiconductor sales reached $517.7 billion in the third quarter of 2026, up 146.8 percent from the third quarter of 2025. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/semiconductor-market-continues-to-accelerate-in-q3-2026/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=semiconductor-market-continues-to-accelerate-in-q3-2026)

**Intel Says EMIB Wafer Utilization Tops 90% as AI Chips Drive 70-Bridge Era: BigGo Finance**
Intel says EMIB wafer utilization tops 90 percent as AI chips drive what it calls a 70-bridge era. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/c626509b-4130-4af6-9c86-fe5c722dfafd)

**GlobalFoundries Data Center Sales Up 81% Ahead of TSMC Deal: FourWeekMBA**
GlobalFoundries’ data-center sales are up 81 percent ahead of a TSMC deal. Source: [fourweekmba.com](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-globalfoundries-data-center-sales-up-81-ahead-of-tsmc-deal/)

**Silicon Photonics Hits the Big Time: EE Times**
EE Times reports a land grab in silicon photonics aimed at the power wall of copper interconnects, including a $125 million funding round for Salience Labs’ optical circuit switching. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/silicon-photonics-hits-the-big-time/)

**DIGITIMES Insight: TSMC, ASML's 2031 photomask target puts High NA EUV suppliers on the clock: digitimes**
DIGITIMES reports that a TSMC and ASML photomask target for 2031 puts High NA EUV suppliers on the clock. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261104PD234/asml-tsmc-euv-photomask-digitimes.html)

### The Teardown: When the Unterminated Link Runs Out of Millimetres
A die-to-die wire inside an advanced package is not a shorter version of a board trace. Semiconductor Engineering, in a system-level signal-integrity piece by Muhammad Hassan, Mahmoud Mahany, and Mohamed Saleh, treats the channel as a stack of discontinuities: microbumps, through-silicon vias, redistribution layers, a silicon interposer or a silicon bridge, then the package transition into the next die. Each of those steps changes impedance and disturbs the return path. At multi-gigahertz rates the loss on those microscopic wires is dominated by skin effect, so insertion loss falls steeply and almost linearly with frequency. The same channel also changes character. At low frequency it behaves like a resistive-capacitive lump. At high frequency it behaves like a transmission line. That shift disperses the edge, spreads symbols into their neighbors, and shows up at the receiver pad as a shorter eye and more jitter.

Crosstalk, not the dielectric, is the louder noise source. Routing gaps of 0.5 micrometres to 2 micrometres let capacitive and inductive coupling inject more noise than the physical dielectric attenuates. The copper itself is on that same scale: traces of 0.5 to 2 micrometres, embedded in deposited silicon dioxide or a low-k film that the foundry has planarized flat, because any waviness misaligns the mask and snaps the wire. A conventional board, by contrast, tolerates thickness variation and uses coarse geometries above 50 micrometres. Checking the die, the interposer, and the package as three separate models misses the coupling that only exists when they are stacked.

Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express is the spec that turns that physics into two different electrical contracts. Semiconductor Engineering walks the split. Advanced packaging, the 2.5D interposer or bridge tier, is specified for an ultra-short reach of 2 millimetres or less, at up to 64 gigatransfers per second per pin under UCIe 3.0, with 64 single-ended mainband data lanes per module. Those signals are left unterminated at the receiver, and the energy target is 0.25 picojoules per bit. Standard packaging, the 2D laminate tier, stretches the channel to 25 millimetres, at 16 to 32 gigatransfers per second per pin, across 16 single-ended mainband lanes per module. The receiver uses 50-ohm parallel ground terminations to kill reflections off the longer trace, and the energy cost is 0.5 picojoules per bit. Physical-layer latency on the open spec is described as up to sub-2 nanoseconds. Compliance is not a lab courtesy: the extracted insertion loss, S21, has to stay strictly above a mandatory voltage-transfer-function mask.

Take the energy numbers as a worked budget, using only those published targets. One bit on the advanced-package path is budgeted at 0.25 picojoules. The same bit on the laminate path is budgeted at 0.5 picojoules, twice the energy, because the termination has to absorb the reflection the short unterminated link never builds up. A module on the advanced path also carries 64 mainband lanes against 16 on the standard path, four times the lane count, at a peak rate of 64 gigatransfers per second against a standard-package band of 16 to 32. The bargain is the reach. Two millimetres is the advanced-package ceiling in that description; 25 millimetres is what the terminated laminate is allowed to span. Stretch the unterminated, 0.25-picojoule link toward that longer run and the reflection the termination was invented to kill comes back, the eye that already lost height to the linear roll-off closes further, and the S21 curve fails the mask even if the arithmetic of the link still “works” on a short channel.

The unterminated advanced-package choice stops being the right electrical design once the physical span leaves that 2-millimetre reach, or once a bump map cannot keep aggressors inside the 0.5-to-2-micrometre gap regime without the coupling exceeding dielectric loss. At that point the designer is on the standard-package contract: fewer lanes, a lower transfer rate, a 50-ohm termination, and 0.5 picojoules per bit. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/a-system-level-approach-to-protecting-3d-ic-signal-integrity/)

### On the Horizon
- Around May or June 2027: Musk’s stated aim for a test chip operating at an Austin research fab tied to the Terafab plan.
- 2029: first heat delivery expected under atNorth’s Calentix reuse deal at SWE04 in Sollefteå.
- 2038: the coal-use extension Arizona Public Service has proposed in the integrated resource plan filed Friday.
- 2031: the TSMC and ASML photomask target DIGITIMES says now clocks High NA EUV suppliers.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **TSMC expects A16 volume production in 2027, a year ahead of Intel's 14A.**

**What You Need to Know:** TSMC expects A16 volume production in 2027, a year ahead of Intel's planned 14A high-volume ramp. The node is the company's first with Super Power Rail backside power delivery, and it is not using High-NA EUV to get there. AMD's data-center revenue nearly doubled in the same stretch, on Instinct MI450 and EPYC.

### Top Story
Startup Fortune reports that TSMC expects its A16 process, a 1.6-nanometer-class node aimed at high-performance computing with complex signal routing and dense power delivery, to be ready in 2026, with customer product ramps pointing to volume production in 2027. Compared with TSMC's N2P, the company puts A16 at 8 to 10 percent faster performance at the same power, or 15 to 20 percent less power at the same speed, plus roughly 8 to 10 percent higher transistor density. A16 is TSMC's first process to use Super Power Rail, which moves the power-delivery network to the back of the wafer instead of routing it with the signal wires on the front. The report says TSMC is reaching that node without ASML's High-NA EUV tools, which run north of 350 million euros each; at an earlier briefing, Zhang's line was "I like the technology but I don't like the sticker price." On the roadmaps in that account, A16 volume would begin about a year before Intel's planned 14A ramp — Lip-Bu Tan has said the company is fully committed to high-volume 14A production in 2028, with risk production for internal chips in the second half of 2027 — and about two years before Samsung's SF1.4 mass-production target of 2029, two years later than the target Samsung announced in 2022. TSMC says it plans to more than double annual N2-family capacity in 2027 for smartphone and HPC demand; supply-chain reporting indicates much of the initial N2 capacity has been heavily booked. Source: [startupfortune.com](https://startupfortune.com/tsmcs-a16-chip-process-is-arriving-early-and-intel-cant-catch-up/)

### Silicon
**AMD Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results: AMD**
AMD's third-quarter release put revenue at a record $13.4 billion, up 45 percent year over year, with GAAP gross margin of 54 percent, operating income of $2.8 billion, net income of $2.4 billion and diluted earnings per share of $1.46; non-GAAP figures were a 56 percent gross margin, $3.9 billion of operating income, $3.5 billion of net income and $2.09 of diluted earnings per share, the last up 74 percent year over year. Data Center revenue was a record $8.5 billion, up 97 percent year over year, on EPYC processors and the launch of Instinct MI450 Series GPUs. Client and Gaming revenue was $3.7 billion, down 8 percent: client revenue was $2.9 billion, up 7 percent on Ryzen mobile, while gaming revenue was $773 million, down 40 percent on lower semi-custom and graphics sales; Embedded revenue was $1.1 billion, up 29 percent. Lisa Su said demand for Instinct and EPYC kept strengthening and that growth should accelerate in the fourth quarter as AMD scales Helios and Venice production. Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure are running workloads on the first Helios rack-scale systems, with MI450 GPUs and 6th Gen EPYC CPUs; HPE said Vultr will deploy the first Helios by HPE systems, and OCI said its Compute E7 instances will use 6th Gen EPYC. AMD also announced an agreement to acquire Taalas for specialized inference silicon, and the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking selected Instinct MI430X GPUs and 6th Gen EPYC processors for the LUMI-AI supercomputer. Source: [ir.amd.com](https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1303/amd-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results)

**Intel Releases 0.9 PDK for 14A Node, Final Version in Q1 2027: TechPowerUp**
In late October Intel released process design kit version 0.9 for the 14A node. Lip-Bu Tan called that kit the "holy grail" because customers can evaluate the node and start trial designs that can move into production with PDK 1.0, which Intel expects in the first quarter of 2027. The company has processed tens of thousands of 14A wafers in pilot runs and is working yield and minor node adjustments. Against 18A, 14A is designed for a 15 to 20 percent performance gain at the same power, or a 25 to 35 percent power cut at the same performance, with up to a 30 percent density improvement; TechPowerUp notes it is unclear whether that density figure is logic or SRAM. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354442/intel-releases-0-9-pdk-for-14a-node-final-version-in-q1-2027)

**ARIA’s Scaling Inference Lab Deploys Lumai’s Optical Compute Tech: HPCwire**
HPCwire reports that the UK's Advanced Research and Invention Agency will deploy 3D optical inference technology from Oxford-based Lumai in ARIA's Scaling Inference Lab. Lumai says it uses light to perform AI inference to lower data-center power consumption by 90 percent and unlock 50 times higher processing speeds. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/arias-scaling-inference-lab-deploys-lumais-optical-compute-tech/)

### Data Centres & Power

TerraVolt has announced a 240 megawatt gas-powered behind-the-meter data-center campus after acquiring 1,077 acres in Cassia County, Idaho. California Resources and Bloom Energy are eyeing 1 gigawatt of fuel cells across California to power data centers and other offtakers. Small outsourced assembly and test firms in India can start with 1.5 to 2 billion rupees, about $15.8 to $21 million, consultant Nitin Dodia said.
