# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Micron's forty-four billion dollar quarter covers its fab spending without new outside cash.**

**What You Need to Know:** Micron's forty-four billion dollar quarter covers its fab spending without new outside cash. Chief financial officer Mark Murphy put fiscal fourth-quarter operating cash flow at $44 billion, capital spending at $10.8 billion, and free cash flow at $33.2 billion, with $12.3 billion of customer deposits in the same quarter. A year earlier, the quarter ended August 28, 2025, produced $5.73 billion of operating cash flow.

### Top Story
Micron chief financial officer Mark Murphy said fiscal fourth-quarter operating cash flow was $44 billion, capital expenditures were $10.8 billion, and free cash flow was $33.2 billion, as reported from the earnings call by shattered.io. The quarter ended August 28, 2025, had produced $5.73 billion of operating cash flow, about 7.7 times lower than the new figure. Operating cash flow for all of fiscal 2025 was $17.53 billion, so this one quarter is about 2.5 times that full year. Murphy said customer cash deposits received during fiscal Q4 were $12.3 billion. Adjusted free cash flow in the year-earlier quarter was $803 million, and shattered.io notes that figure carries an "adjusted" label while the new free-cash-flow remark does not, so the definitions may not match. Micron's investor-relations notice scheduled the fiscal fourth-quarter report for September 30, 2026. Source: [shattered.io](https://shattered.io/micron-q4-cash-flow-44-billion-vhbm-roadmap-2026/)

### Silicon
**SK Hynix vs. Micron: Wall Street Sees Roughly Equal Upside in the Memory Duopoly: BigGo Finance**
On October 22, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang told CNBC he does not anticipate a memory surplus by 2029. In the second quarter, SK Hynix held 25 percent of DRAM, 50 percent of HBM, and 19 percent of NAND, while Micron held 24 percent of DRAM, 18 percent of HBM, and 15 percent of NAND. Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 379 percent year over year and gross margin expanded to 86.8 percent from 44.7 percent; SK Hynix grew revenue 257 percent and lifted gross margin to 83 percent from 54 percent. Both draw about 73 percent of sales from DRAM. Nvidia and SK Hynix signed a long-term partnership in July valued at more than $500 billion covering memory supply and AI data-center buildouts. Micron has 26 long-term agreements covering more than 35 percent of revenue through 2030. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/a918e668-2399-418a-b1e9-bb5e06fb81b7)

**Amazon's Trainium Takes a Strike at the Training King: SemiAnalysis**
Anthropic is running production inference and reinforcement-learning rollouts on Trainium2 and Trainium3. SemiAnalysis says its engineering team has been on Trainium3 racks for a couple of weeks. The team found bugs and says the stack is nowhere close to CUDA's maturity, while calling the direction right. Trainium uses up to 80,000 physical cores allocated to automated quality control. Source: [newsletter.semianalysis.com](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/amazons-trainium-takes-a-strike-at)

**AMD Lists Three Zen 6 Medusa GPU IDs in HIPRT 3.2: TechPowerUp**
AMD's HIPRT 3.2 release notes name Medusa integrated-graphics support for architecture IDs gfx1170, gfx1171, and gfx115E. The gfx117x IDs belong to RDNA 4m, which sits in the GFX11 family with RDNA 3 and 3.5 and adds FP8/BF8 conversion and new matrix instructions. GFX1171 and GFX1172 targets were added in March after the IDs showed up in LLVM in February; GFX1171 was merged into Mesa 26.3 in August, with RDNA 4m firmware later that month. GFX115x covers RDNA 3.5 graphics in Strix Point and Strix Halo, so gfx115E reads as at least one Medusa chip staying on RDNA 3.5. HIPRT is used by rendering apps such as Blender, and the notes are not a gaming-performance claim. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354085/amd-lists-three-zen-6-medusa-gpu-ids-in-hiprt-3-2)

### Data Centres & Power
**Meta details Ohio Prometheus data center campus, with first phase live: Data Center Dynamics**
Meta's Prometheus campus in Ohio is energized in its first phase, which Data Center Dynamics reports as already live. The campus has already been used to train Muse. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/meta-details-ohio-prometheus-data-center-campus-with-first-phase-live/)

**Oregon city declares state of emergency over lost data center revenue amid state-wide ban: Data Center Dynamics**
The city of Umatilla, Oregon, has declared a state of emergency over lost data-center revenue amid a statewide ban. The city was relying on tax revenue due from Sabey and Amazon. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/oregon-city-declares-state-of-emergency-over-lost-data-center-revenue-amid-state-wide-ban/)

**ZTE unveils data center module designed for AI workloads: Data Center Dynamics**
ZTE has unveiled a data-center module designed for AI workloads. Rack power inside the module will range from 20 kilowatts to 60 kilowatts. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/zte-unveils-data-center-module-designed-for-ai-workloads/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Solidigm confirms plans to build a fab in the US, abandons IPO plans: Tom's Hardware**
SK hynix has abandoned IPO plans for Solidigm and confirmed plans to build a Solidigm 3D NAND fab in the United States, citing unfavorable stock-market conditions and semiconductor share-price trends. BigGo Finance reports the company suspended its review of a potential U.S. listing that reports had suggested could raise as much as $15 billion, said Solidigm's growth prospects and investment needs are unchanged, and said it will keep exploring other funding. eToro APAC analyst Josh Gilbert said the move removes a governance worry and keeps Solidigm's value inside the company. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/ssds/solidigm-confirms-plans-to-build-a-fab-in-the-us-abandons-ipo-plans-unfavorable-stock-market-conditions-and-semiconductor-share-price-trends-reasons-given) · [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/a918e668-2399-418a-b1e9-bb5e06fb81b7)

**Arm Comments on Jury Decision in Qualcomm Trial: EE Times**
Arm chief marketing officer Ami Badani told EE Times the jury's $2 nominal damages award validates Arm's position in the Qualcomm case. The jury awarded $1 for a licensing breach and $1 for interference with Qualcomm's business relationship with Meta, and found for Arm on other allegations. Judge Maryellen Noreika called Qualcomm's request that the court compel good-faith talks on Arm's v10 architecture "very, very drastic." Badani said a final written ruling on the remaining antitrust and licensing claims could take several weeks. She said RISC-V is not obtaining meaningful traction outside China, and attributed its growth there to state backing rather than commercial displacement. Qualcomm has acquired RISC-V startup Akeana, and Barcelona Supercomputing Center director Mateo Valero told EE Times that closed instruction sets such as Arm limit designers' freedom to add functions and cut power. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/arm-comments-on-jury-decision-in-qualcomm-trial/)

**TSMC to give NT$30,000 Sports Day bonus despite event canceled due to typhoon: Focus Taiwan**
TSMC will pay each non-managerial employee a Sports Day bonus of NT$30,000 (US$923) even though Typhoon Champi forced cancellation of Saturday's event. Chairman and chief executive C.C. Wei said in a Friday internal email that the 2026 bonus is NT$5,000 higher than last year's. It will be distributed in November to employees on the payroll as of May 31, 2026. Last year the company paid NT$25,000, including overseas employees for the first time, and distributed about NT$1.875 billion in such bonuses in 2025. TSMC posted NT$2.42 trillion in net profit in the first nine months of this year, up 68.5 percent from a year earlier. At an October 15 investor conference it forecast 2026 sales up 44 percent in U.S. dollar terms, versus a July view of slightly higher than 40 percent. Source: [focustaiwan.tw](https://focustaiwan.tw/business/202610240008)

**Atomera, IQE Partner on RF GaN-on-Silicon for Volume Markets: Semiconductor Digest**
Atomera and IQE will co-optimize MST-enabled gallium-nitride-on-silicon wafers for radio-frequency volume markets. IQE will manufacture the wafers for foundry and integrated-device-manufacturer customers. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/atomera-iqe-partner-on-rf-gan-on-silicon-for-volume-markets/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=atomera-iqe-partner-on-rf-gan-on-silicon-for-volume-markets)

### The Teardown: Why Backside Power Lets One Exposure Finish the Pitch
High numerical aperture extreme ultraviolet lithography raises the resolution of the light on a wafer until the printable pitch, the space between two features, sits between 16 nanometres and 8 nanometres. Wccftech's account of Intel vice president Chris Auth, speaking on the Dwarkesh podcast, is that a pitch in that window can be printed in a single exposure. One pass is the cost argument: one mask, one alignment, one dose. When a design needs a tighter pitch than one exposure can hold, a foundry prints the pattern in stages. Each stage only has to hit a looser pitch. The exposures together make the dense pattern. That second exposure is double-patterning EUV. It spends a second pass, a second mask, and an overlay budget between the two.

Backside power delivery is how Auth says Intel stays inside the single-pass window. Power wires move off the front of the wafer and onto the back. The front, where the computing transistors sit and where the circuits that move data between them sit, no longer shares that space with the power grid. Auth's claim is that this relaxes the front-side pitch enough to print that level directly with high numerical aperture tools. A looser pitch also relaxes the error tolerance, because features do not have to land as close together. He contrasts that with TSMC, which he says must run tighter pitches because it does not have backside power, cannot print that layer with high numerical aperture in one pass, and has to use double-patterning EUV.

Take those pitch numbers as a gate. If the front side still needs a pitch between 16 nanometres and 8 nanometres, Auth's account says one high numerical aperture exposure can print it. If the pitch has to be tighter than 8 nanometres, that single exposure is outside its window and the flow falls back to two EUV passes. Intel's bet is that moving power to the back keeps the front-side pitch inside the 16-to-8 window, so the second pass never starts. Auth added that 14A is an option in the process design kit today, handled customer by customer. That is narrower than a general release. Earlier reports, which his comments are described as moving past, had discussed backside power on 18A. The scanner choice and the node name are separate: in his telling, high numerical aperture pays only where backside power has already bought the pitch relief.

Chief technology officer Pushkar Ranade, on the same podcast, separates that lithography claim from scale. He said TSMC is a much larger wafer manufacturer today, and that catching up in scale will be slow and gradual. On technology he said Intel is already there, maybe a few percent off on performance or power or area density. A gap of a few percent, he argued, is a different problem from being a whole generation behind. The condition he put first is time and yield. You can be off by a few percent, but you need to be on time, and yields have to be very high to support very large and very rapid ramps. A one-pass exposure that prints inside 8 to 16 nanometres still loses the ramp if yield cannot fill a fast volume curve while the larger foundry is already shipping.

A second failure mode sits in the transistor stack, not in the scanner. Wccftech quotes Intel's Jack Kavalieros on stacking n-type and p-type transistors, the approach IBM has tied to a 0.7-nanometre plan. Connections that used to run on the top, or on the bottom, now have to go vertically between the transistors. The trenches that carry those connections get taller relative to their width. Filling them gets harder. Unfilled trenches leave air gaps and holes. Backside power can free the front side for a single high numerical aperture pass and still be the wrong process once those vertical interconnects, not the in-plane pitch, set the yield. Source: [wccftech.com](https://wccftech.com/intel-tech-chief-says-it-is-only-a-few-percent-behind-tsmc-on-performance-but-catching-up-in-scale-will-be-slow-vp-asserts-high-na-euv-is-the-right-choice/)

### On the Horizon
- November 2026: TSMC distributes the NT$30,000 Sports Day bonus to employees who were on the payroll as of May 31, 2026.
- Within several weeks: Arm expects a final written ruling on the remaining antitrust and licensing claims in the Qualcomm case.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Amazon scraps four Loudoun data centers, turning 122 acres toward housing.**

**What You Need to Know:** Amazon scraps four Loudoun data centers, turning 122 acres toward housing. The former George Washington University campus will mostly become mixed-use and residential land, with 25 acres and $5 million going to the county. Kazakhstan’s licensed GPU build, a split over the next DRAM cell, and a new gas-engine order fill the rest of the day.

### Top Story
Tom's Hardware reports that Amazon will not build four new data centers on the former George Washington University campus in Loudoun County, just outside Washington, D.C. Most of the 122-acre property is to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. Amazon will donate 25 acres to Loudoun County for a community arts center and a recreational facility, and give $5 million to the county’s housing fund. The company submitted the data-center proposal in July and met Board of Supervisors Chair Phyllis J. Randall in September. Josh Weissman, Amazon’s vice president for data center development, said the county had “pointed concerns about data center development at this particular site,” and that “the best outcome for all is to come together on a shared vision for this campus rather than engage in costly litigation.” Randall said the agreement will “provide more attainable homes for working families.” Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/amazon-bows-to-local-backlash-over-ai-data-centers-scraps-plans-to-build-four-new-facilities-in-northern-virginia-site-to-be-repurposed-for-mixed-use-and-residential-development)

### Silicon
**YMTC to Start Mass Production of LPDDR5X with 9,600 MT/s Speed: TechPowerUp**
YMTC is preparing volume production of LPDDR5X at 9,600 MT/s at Fab 3, using a vertical-channel-transistor 4F² cell. Counterpoint Research says the company has made about 5,000 wafers a month of 16 Gb LPDDR5X at 7,500 MT/s at Fab 2 since October 2025. Xtacking 4.0 separates the memory-cell wafer from peripheral logic and joins them by hybrid bonding. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354058/ymtc-to-start-mass-production-of-lpddr5x-with-9-600-mt-s-speed)

**Micron Walks Away From 4F² DRAM After Two Decades of Research, Bets on 3D DRAM Instead: TechPowerUp**
Scott DeBoer, Micron’s president and chief technology and products officer, said on an October 21 webinar that Micron will not bring 4F² DRAM to market. On paper the cell cuts footprint by about a third versus today’s 6F² layout, but DeBoer said real density is limited by how tightly capacitors pack, and that 4F² costs more and runs into scaling limits at leading-edge nodes. Samsung and SK hynix are still developing 4F², and CXMT says its first 4F² product, a server DDR5 RDIMM, is due by the end of this year. Micron will keep scaling 6F², with the 1-delta node set to ramp in Boise in the second half of 2027 and 1-epsilon after that moving to wafer bonding. 3D DRAM is a parallel path with no timeline, and Micron says it will switch only when the economics make sense. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354042/micron-walks-away-from-4f-dram-after-two-decades-of-research-bets-on-3d-dram-instead)

**LattePanda Launches LattePanda Sigma 2: The Embeddable AI Single Board Server: TechPowerUp**
LattePanda launched the Sigma 2, an x86 single-board server built on the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H with Intel Arc B390 graphics. The board is rated at up to 180 TOPS of total AI performance at INT8 and supports up to 64 GB of memory. It is meant to sit inside the product — robots, vision systems, instruments, private AI appliances — rather than beside it. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353798/lattepanda-launches-lattepanda-sigma-2-the-embeddable-ai-single-board-server)

### Data Centres & Power
**NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure expanding in Kazakhstan: NVIDIA Blog**
Firebird’s first phase in Kazakhstan is under construction at Data Center Valley, and a planned second phase would take total potential capacity to about 500 megawatts. Firebird has a U.S. export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs; commercial launch of the first phase, built with Kazakhtelecom, is targeted for the third quarter of 2027, and Firebird plans Firebird Labs Kazakhstan for local startups and research. The investment-agreement signing at the presidential palace coincided with Jensen Huang’s October 23 visit to Astana and his meeting with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Kazakhtelecom has already deployed 400 NVIDIA H200 and 480 NVIDIA B300 GPUs in Astana and Almaty. Next year it plans more than 1,000 GPUs at Data Center Valley and more than 1,000 NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs in the Ekibastuz region. Huang said that “instead of just exporting energy, in the future, you could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence.” Source: [blogs.nvidia.com](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/kazakhstan-ai-compute-ecosystem/)

**Crusoe to develop 106MW data center site in Paraguay: Data Center Dynamics**
Crusoe’s Paraguay data center site is announced at 106 megawatts, developed with partner Araico. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/crusoe-to-develop-106mw-data-center-site-in-paraguay/)

**Innio signs 620MW gas engine order with undisclosed US data center developer: Data Center Dynamics**
Innio has signed a 620-megawatt gas-engine order with an undisclosed U.S. data center developer. The order builds on a 1.1-gigawatt order signed in July. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/innio-signs-620mw-gas-engine-order-with-undisclosed-us-data-center-developer/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**FCC issues first bans under new chip-level rule: Tom's Hardware**
The FCC has issued its first bans under a new chip-level rule, covering a dashcam and a wireless video transmitter from HiSilicon, a Huawei subsidiary. The ban is tied to an AI chip that advertises face-detection algorithms. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/cyber-security/fcc-bans-first-two-devices-from-the-us-under-new-chip-level-rule-huawei-subsidiary-chip-boasts-face-detection-algorithm)

**Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs found inside state-owned China Telecom's network: Tom's Hardware**
Tom's Hardware reports that a security firm identified 32 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra B300 chips running inside a China Telecom network. Where those export-barred parts physically sit is unclear. NVIDIA’s position, as carried in the report, is that chip smuggling is a drop in the bucket and remains a nonfactor. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/illegal-nvidia-blackwell-ultra-b300-gpus-found-inside-state-owned-china-telecoms-network-nvidia-says-chip-smuggling-a-drop-in-the-bucket-insists-smuggling-remains-a-nonfactor)

**US Department of Commerce commits up to $389m in R&D funding to power semiconductors for fusion and advanced computing: Data Center Dynamics**
The U.S. Department of Commerce has committed up to $389 million in R&D funding for power semiconductors aimed at fusion and advanced computing. Google-backed CFS and Microsoft-backed Helion are set to receive R&D funding. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/us-department-of-commerce-commits-up-to-389m-in-rd-funding-to-power-semiconductors-for-fusion-and-advanced-computing/)

**QumulusAI Expands Equipment Lease Financing With Tech Finance Co. To $123.6 Million For NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs: Pulse 2.0**
QumulusAI expanded an equipment lease with Tech Finance Co. to about $123.6 million, up from $26 million announced in May 2026, to fund NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs the company said it was buying in May and July 2026. TFC finances about 85 to 90 percent of equipment cost on each schedule; customer deposits cover the rest. The leases run three years at a high-single-digit annualized interest rate, and QumulusAI can buy the hardware at the end or return it. Chief executive Michael Maniscalco said the hardware is paid for by contracted demand rather than by shareholders. Source: [pulse2.com](https://pulse2.com/qumulusai-expands-equipment-lease-financing-with-tech-finance-co-to-123-6-million-for-nvidia-blackwell-gpus/)

### Also Today
**Gigaphoton Takes Its Lightsources Beyond the Scanner: Semiconductor Digest**
Gigaphoton is taking its excimer-laser work into micro-via drilling for advanced packaging, compact EUV sources for actinic mask inspection and 3D metrology, and on-site neon recycling. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/gigaphoton-takes-its-lightsources-beyond-the-scanner/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=gigaphoton-takes-its-lightsources-beyond-the-scanner)

**Two Dollars and a Test Suite: EE Times**
A $2 damages award in the Arm-Qualcomm case drew the headlines, but EE Times says the larger issue is who controls the compliance tests a custom chip must pass before it ships. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/two-dollars-and-a-test-suite/)

**NVIDIA Pushes Toward the “AI-Defined Fab”: Semiconductor Digest**
Chipmakers, equipment suppliers and EDA companies are adopting NVIDIA’s CUDA-X libraries and AI tools for what NVIDIA calls AI-defined fabs, tying accelerated simulation, AI physics, AI agents and digital twins across the factory. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/nvidia-pushes-toward-the-ai-defined-fab/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=nvidia-pushes-toward-the-ai-defined-fab)

### The Teardown: When the Fourth Mask Loses the Exposure
A dense layer does not have to be drawn in a single pass. Break the pattern into simpler pieces, expose each piece on a deep-ultraviolet scanner, and the stack can approximate a feature that one shot of that light cannot print. Tom's Hardware put that workaround to Chris Mack, co-founder and chief technology officer of Fractilia, because export rules have kept ASML’s extreme-ultraviolet tools out of China. Those machines print with 13.5-nanometre light. Without them, the path left is older deep-ultraviolet lithography plus multiple patterning.

What that path has already printed is in shipping phones. A teardown of Huawei’s Mate 60 Pro found the Kirin 9000S made by SMIC on a second-generation 7-nanometre-class process with no EUV. Later analysis of the Kirin 9030 found SMIC’s DUV flow pushed closer to densities associated with 5-nanometre manufacturing, while still lagging the leading processes at TSMC and Samsung. Mack’s point is that a node label hides the cost of getting there. Every added exposure has to land on patterns already etched. More masks mean more overlay error and more process variation. Designers buy a printable layer by leaving extra space around features. The die grows. A larger die means fewer candidates on each wafer, and wafers cost tens of thousands of dollars. The thing sold is the good die, not the wafer.

Mack’s cost line is the worked case. He told Tom's Hardware that industry convention held three exposures on an immersion tool at about the same cost as one EUV exposure. At four masks standing in for that single EUV exposure, EUV becomes the cheaper shot, and the cleaner one, because four overlay stacks accumulate defects one exposure never introduces. Memory shows the same gap in a June Morgan Stanley estimate: CXMT was producing only about one-third as many bits per wafer as Western competitors. Analysts put only about a third of that shortfall on the older process node and called lithography access a hard ceiling. Micron’s 1-alpha DRAM, built without EUV, is the counter-example — competitive chips from deep-ultraviolet light, multiple patterning and tight control, while Samsung and SK hynix used many EUV layers for the same generation. Douglas Fuller of Copenhagen Business School told Tom's Hardware that other routes around EUV for advanced logic are unlikely to be efficient, and that by the end of the decade advanced packaging could still let DUV print the latest DRAM generations.

Four masks against one EUV exposure is where this choice stops paying for a logic layer. Overlay error, a fatter die and fewer good dice per wafer then dominate the scanner that was never delivered. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/china-can-make-advanced-chips-without-euv-but-the-bill-keeps-growing-duv-multiple-patterning-means-bigger-dies-lower-yields-and-longer-manufacturing-times)

### On the Horizon
- Firebird is targeting commercial launch of its first Kazakhstan phase in the third quarter of 2027.
- Kazakhtelecom plans, next year, more than 1,000 GPUs at Data Center Valley and more than 1,000 Vera Rubin GPUs in Ekibastuz.
- Micron’s 1-delta DRAM node is set to ramp in Boise in the second half of 2027.
- CXMT says its first 4F² product, a server DDR5 RDIMM, is due by the end of this year.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **NVIDIA plans a 2.5-times substrate build so AI factory capacity can actually ship.**

**What You Need to Know:** NVIDIA has announced a 2.5-times increase in substrate capacity over three years, with named partners expanding packaging, test and optical engines. Samsung and SK hynix are pointing the memory roadmap at stacked HBM and a finished HBM4 design, while a one-gigawatt solid-state-transformer order and a wafer-shipment forecast set the supply picture around the chips.

### Top Story
NVIDIA announced plans with Amkor Technology, IBIDEN, King Yuan Electronics, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Siliconware Precision Industries and Unimicron to expand substrates, advanced packaging, testing and optical engines for its AI factory platform. Jensen Huang said demand is extraordinary and capacity is the constraint. Substrate capacity is planned to rise 2.5 times over the next three years: under an agreement IBIDEN signed and announced earlier this year, NVIDIA is providing a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation advance for the Ono Plant in Japan, targeting three times current levels there; Samsung Electro-Mechanics is joining from existing South Korean lines, with upgrades and new factories in Sejong and Busan; and NVIDIA is backing Unimicron’s KF substrate expansion in Taiwan with a capacity reservation. With Amkor, the plan targets a greater than 300 percent increase in interposer wafer capacity in South Korea by the end of 2028. NVIDIA expects total semiconductor testing capacity to double from calendar 2026 to 2027, including a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to King Yuan Electronics for new U.S. testing facilities and equipment, with further buildouts in Taiwan and Singapore. With SPIL, manufacturing capacity in Taiwan for optical engines used in co-packaged optics is targeted to rise 15 times. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/nvidia-and-supply-chain-partners-expand-capacity-to-accelerate-ai-infrastructure-buildout/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=nvidia-and-supply-chain-partners-expand-capacity-to-accelerate-ai-infrastructure-buildout)
Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353982/nvidia-and-supply-chain-partners-expand-capacity-to-accelerate-ai-infrastructure-buildout)

### Silicon
**What Samsung Unveiled at FMS 2026: zHBM, zNAND-O and V10 BV-NAND: shattered.io**
At FMS 2026 in Santa Clara on August 4, Samsung showed three memory concepts rather than a shipping flagship, shattered.io reports from Samsung’s technical announcement. zHBM stacks memory vertically above the accelerator instead of placing HBM beside it on an interposer. Kim Kyoung-ryun said zHBM delivers up to eight times the performance per GPU and up to three times the performance per watt compared with HBM5, a generation that has not reached commercial shipment. zNAND-O, in four- and eight-layer versions of stacked V-NAND with through-silicon vias, is aimed at on-device AI, and V10 bonding-vertical NAND is described as exceeding 400 layers. SK hynix, in the same write-up, says it has finished HBM4 development and is preparing mass production. Source: [shattered.io](https://shattered.io/what-samsung-unveiled-at-fms-2026-zhbm-znand-o-and-v10-bv-nand/)

**Navitas Unveils Next-Generation Ultra-High-Voltage SiC Power Module: Semiconductor Digest**
Navitas announced the G4H08MT23GB4, a 2300-volt full-bridge silicon-carbide module in the SiCPAK form factor with an on-resistance of 8 milliohms, and said samples are available immediately. The part extends a 2300-volt and 3300-volt GeneSiC portfolio and is aimed at solid-state transformers that take grid power to the high-voltage DC rails inside AI data-centre racks, as well as grid storage, solar inverters and megawatt EV charging. An aluminum-nitride active-metal-braze substrate supports isolation of over 5 kilovolts, and epoxy-resin potting is described as delivering 10 times the thermal conductivity of silicone gel. Press-fit pins are rated at twice the current per pin of standard press-fit connections, with optional pre-applied thermal interface material and high-current pin variants. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/navitas-unveils-next-generation-ultra-high-voltage-sic-power-module/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=navitas-unveils-next-generation-ultra-high-voltage-sic-power-module)

**NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026 NVIDIA Intros DSX PODs and More: ServeTheHome**
ServeTheHome reports that NVIDIA introduced the DSX POD at GTC Berlin 2026 as a server-in-a-container, alongside software updates for its ecosystem. Arm, writing about the same system, calls a drop from six months to as little as 14 days the potential leap in AI factory deployment speed. The POD is described as powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure built on Arm-based Vera CPUs. That 14-day figure is a potential deployment claim, not a recorded fleet install. Source: [servethehome.com](https://www.servethehome.com/nvidia-gtc-berlin-2026-nvidia-intros-dsx-pods-and-more/)
Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Arm/status/2113015866996727821)

**Leak: Intel Core Ultra 9 4995HX Leads Nova Lake Laptop Lineup: TechPowerUp**
TechPowerUp, citing leaker Jaykihn, reports that the Core Ultra 9 4995HX uses an 8+16+4+2 layout — 28 CPU cores, four more than current Arrow Lake-HX — and that Intel has not confirmed the part. The same post lists the Core Ultra 9 4970H as 4+8+4+12, for 16 CPU cores and a 12-core Xe3P graphics block. Jaykihn put the final 8+16 HX compute tile, on TSMC N2P, at 14.8 by 6.6 millimetres, about 98 square millimetres. Current reports point to the first Nova Lake-H and HX laptops around CES 2027, treated as tentative. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353986/leak-intel-core-ultra-9-4995hx-leads-nova-lake-laptop-lineup)

### Data Centres & Power
**Data Centers Can Delay, Not Dodge, the Power Crunch: Data Center Knowledge**
An Infosys analysis of AI energy demand through 2030, reported by Data Center Knowledge, argues that efficiency and flexible workloads can free usable capacity sooner than new generation, transmission and grid upgrades, without removing the need for that infrastructure. Mit Majumdar of Infosys said those measures are more likely to delay than eliminate new build, and that the path is dual-track: use what exists while accelerating generation, transmission and grid modernization. Model training, retraining and batch work can often move with grid conditions; real-time inference and customer-facing applications generally cannot. Utilities, he said, should require historical performance, real-time monitoring and contractual commitments, with operators guaranteeing claims and utilities setting the verification standard. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/energy-power-supply/data-centers-can-delay-not-dodge-the-power-crunch)

**Vantage signs 1GW solid-state transformer supply deal with Heron Power: Data Center Dynamics**
Vantage has signed a supply deal for 1 gigawatt of Heron Link solid-state transformers from Heron Power, Data Center Dynamics reports. The agreement is a signed equipment order, not an energized site. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/vantage-signs-1gw-solid-state-transformer-supply-deal-with-heron-power/)

**SC Capital Partners invests in 40MW data center in Pohang, South Korea: Data Center Dynamics**
A 40-megawatt data centre in Pohang, South Korea, is under construction in the sense that it is being developed with NeoAI Cloud, after an investment by SC Capital Partners, Data Center Dynamics reports. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/sc-capital-partners-invests-in-40mw-data-center-in-pohang-south-korea/)

**Russian forces destroy GigaCenter data center in Kyiv, Ukraine: Data Center Dynamics**
Data Center Dynamics reports that Russian forces destroyed the GigaCenter data centre in Kyiv, as Ukrainian forces attacked telecoms facilities in Russian-occupied Donetsk and Luhansk. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/russian-forces-destroy-gigacenter-data-center-in-kyiv-ukraine/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**SEMI Forecasts 11.8% Growth in Silicon Wafer Shipments in 2026, With Record Highs Expected through 2029: Semiconductor Digest**
SEMI’s annual silicon shipment forecast, reported by Semiconductor Digest, projects global silicon wafer shipments up 11.8 percent in 2026 to 14,420 million square inches, with record highs expected through 2029. That is a forecast, not a completed shipment year. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/semi-forecasts-11-8-growth-in-silicon-wafer-shipments-in-2026-with-record-highs-expected-through-2029/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=semi-forecasts-11-8-growth-in-silicon-wafer-shipments-in-2026-with-record-highs-expected-through-2029)

**EXCLUSIVE: TSMC seeks factory-equipment alternatives to thwart China's rare earths grip, sources say: Reuters**
Reuters reports, citing sources, that TSMC is seeking factory-equipment alternatives to limit China’s hold on rare earths, a report also carried by Twaslnews. The company has not confirmed the effort in the text available here. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/tsmc-seeks-factory-equipment-alternatives-thwart-chinas-rare-earths-grip-sources-2026-10-22/)
Source: [twaslnews1.twaslnews.com](https://twaslnews1.twaslnews.com/6403353/)

**Intel installs production tools at Fab 62 in Arizona, provides updates on Ohio chip fab: Tom's Hardware**
Tom’s Hardware reports that Intel is installing production tools at Fab 62 in Arizona and confirms high-NA EUV for high-volume manufacturing in 2028. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/semiconductors/intel-installs-production-tools-at-fab-62-in-arizona-provides-updates-on-ohio-chip-fab-confirms-high-na-euv-for-high-volume-manufacturing-in-2028)

**TSMC slows construction after accident kills four: Taipei Times**
Taipei Times reports that TSMC slowed construction after an accident that killed four people. Source: [taipeitimes.com](https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/biz/archives/2026/10/22/2003866386)

### Also Today
**2nm and CoWoS expansion lifts Chi Yi Hsin Technology backlog to NT$4.5B: digitimes**
Digitimes reports that 2-nanometre and CoWoS expansion has lifted Chi Yi Hsin Technology’s backlog to NT$4.5 billion. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261021PD257/expansion-packaging-demand-2026-business.html)

**Micron Unveils Vertical HBM Stacking on GPUs: Chosun**
Chosun reports that Micron unveiled vertical HBM stacking on GPUs. Source: [chosun.com](https://www.chosun.com/english/industry-en/2026/10/22/74VRVD5WXFHI3JI4WMKXOY5BVU/)

**Ryzen 5800X3D Revival was Lisa Su's Initiative, and Other Interesting Details in AMD Interview with MyNavi Tech+: TechPowerUp**
TechPowerUp, from a MyNavi Tech+ interview with Travis Kirsch, reports that reviving the Ryzen 7 5800X3D for Socket AM4 was Lisa Su’s initiative and required TSMC process updates so new chips match the original specs without restarting deprecated processes. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/354011/ryzen-5800x3d-revival-was-lisa-sus-initiative-and-other-interesting-details-in-amd-interview-with-mynavi-tech)

### The Teardown: When the Panel Gives the Count Back
A large AI package is a rectangle, and the workpiece under it has spent decades as a circle. Semiconductor Engineering’s account of the wafer-to-panel shift, drawing on ASE and Intel Foundry engineers, starts from that mismatch. As the package grows, more of a 300-millimetre wafer’s process time lands outside the circle of usable silicon. A panel gives the corners back. It also exposes how much of “the process” was really a habit of the round part: spin, stepper, single-sided handling, a hot plate sized for a wafer.

Teck Chong Lee of ASE put the practical limit in one flow. Running assembly on a 600-millimetre panel is high risk, and the equipment to do the whole job is not all in place. One option is to finish the interposer at 600 millimetres, then cut it into four pieces before assembly and the C4 bump process. The area win is taken where the tools exist, then partly handed back where they do not.

The same study counts a 5.5-times-reticle interposer. A 300-millimetre wafer yields 9. A 300-millimetre panel yields 16. A 600-millimetre panel divided into four 300-millimetre pieces yields 64. Leaving that 600-millimetre panel intact yields 72. Seventy-two against nine is eight times the wafer, more than the roughly fivefold gap in raw area, because the rectangle wastes almost nothing at the rim. Intel’s Tarik Ibrahim, in a conference presentation covered in the same piece, used a 510-by-515-millimetre panel: a package of roughly four times a reticle field is about 10 units on a 300-millimetre wafer and approximately 48 on the panel. The largest square that fits the wafer is only about 210 by 210 millimetres, so past that outline the wafer is not merely less economical. It cannot hold the part.

What breaks is not the arithmetic. At wafer level the process is single-sided. On a panel it is dual-sided, and uniformity and process capability have to hold across a sheet the tools were not born for. Spin coating needs radial symmetry; on a rectangle the film thins toward the corners and most of the resist is thrown off. In a 600-millimetre flow, photoresist goes down by slit or slot-die coating across an active area of roughly 586 by 586 millimetres. Lithography often leaves the wafer stepper for maskless direct imaging. Fine-line redistribution on glass is being pushed from roughly 5 micrometres line and space toward 2 micrometres and below, which asks for something closer to front-end overlay and temperature control. Front-end tools that already do that precision still assume a round 300-millimetre wafer. Older substrate tools were built for coarser features. The panel sits between those two equipment worlds, and neither hands over a complete line.

Ibrahim’s split is the decision rule. For some form factors the wafer is still the cheaper workpiece, because the panel’s extra area does not yet buy extra good units after yield, handling and tool qualification. Past a size the presentation does not pin to a single number, the panel wins because the unit count jumps — 10 to about 48 in Intel’s four-reticle example, 9 to 72 if a 5.5-reticle interposer can stay intact. The intact panel stops being the right workpiece at the step that has no qualified tool. ASE’s four-way cut is that step: assembly and C4. Seventy-two falls to 64, and the rectangles you spent the interposer module earning are sawn back into pieces the existing line can hold. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/what-breaks-when-packaging-moves-from-wafer-to-panel/)

### On the Horizon
- IBIDEN’s additional Ono capacity is expected to begin ramping in the first quarter of 2028, and Unimicron’s KF expansion is expected to start adding capacity in the second quarter of 2027 and reach full capacity by mid-2028.
- King Yuan Electronics high-volume U.S. test production is targeted for April 2027, expanded Singapore testing for February 2027, and SPIL’s optical-engine build is aimed at that 15-times increase by mid-2027 with another doubling by the end of 2028.
- Samsung expects products based on first-generation zHBM after 2029, while it is still defining the first-generation specification.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Four workers died at TSMC's Kaohsiung fab site, halting steel work across Taiwan.**

**What You Need to Know:** Four workers are dead after a steel-structure collapse at TSMC's Fab 22 construction site in Kaohsiung, and the company has stopped similar steel work at its construction sites across Taiwan. Synaptics has announced an edge microcontroller family with on-package DRAM and up to 400 GOPS of AI acceleration. Dell's chief executive says the memory shortage gets worse in 2027, with meaningful new fab supply not expected until 2029 or 2030.

### Top Story
Four workers have died after a steel structure collapsed during a hoisting and installation operation at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co's Fab 22 site in Nanzih District, Kaohsiung, part of the Southern Taiwan Science Park. The Kaohsiung Fire Department received a report at 4:53pm yesterday that four people had been injured; it dispatched 10 vehicles and 22 personnel. Preliminary investigations by the Southern Taiwan Science Park Bureau suggest bolts on a connecting plate of an outer steel structure on the third floor suddenly snapped, and the workers and heavy steel components plunged to the ground. Three workers were pronounced dead last night; the fourth, surnamed Huang, died in intensive care this morning. The four men worked for a domestic contractor. TSMC said it and its construction contractor immediately suspended related construction work at the site, and suspended similar steel structure work at all of its construction sites across Taiwan pending investigation. The bureau has sent labor inspection personnel to determine cause and liability. Fab 22 is scheduled to produce chips on 2-nanometer and more advanced process technologies, with construction of its Phase 4 fab set to be completed next year. Source: [taipeitimes.com](https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2026/10/21/2003866366) Source: [independent.co.uk](https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/east-asia/tsmc-taiwan-factory-accident-workers-killed-b3070397.html)

### Silicon
**Synaptics Announces Astra SR200 Multimodal Edge AI Processors with Google Coral NPU: TechPowerUp**
Synaptics has introduced the Astra SR200 Series, which it calls an xMCU: a microcontroller class meant to run multimodal edge AI that conventional MCUs cannot hold in on-chip memory. The announced parts pair heterogeneous, AI-native compute with integrated high-bandwidth custom DRAM scalable to hundreds of megabytes, so larger models and multimodal workloads can stay on the device. The series uses the Synaptics Torq AI engine and the Coral NPU from Google Research, and Synaptics says it is the first pairing of an Arm Cortex-M85 with a Cortex-M52. EE Times, reporting from Synaptics Tech Day in San Jose on October 20, gives the family up to 400 GOPS of AI acceleration and 256 MB of custom DRAM, with vision, audio, and hardware-rooted security. Three pin-compatible tiers are specified: SR210 at 200 GOPS for always-on voice and sensing, SR230 at 300 GOPS adding vision, display, and optional audio, and SR250 at 400 GOPS with dual vision and display paths. Target devices are AI wearables, battery-powered sensors, connected cameras, streamers, and industrial vision and voice systems; John Weil, vice president and general manager for IoT and edge AI processors, said the strongest traction so far is body-worn electronics. The parts are announced, not described as shipped. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353957/synaptics-announces-astra-sr200-multimodal-edge-ai-processors-with-google-coral-npu) Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/edge-ai-mcu-features-multimodal-compute-tiered-memory/)

**Socionext Expands Agentic AI to Advanced, Large-Scale SoC Physical Design: Semiconductor Digest**
Socionext says it is extending agentic AI from front-end design into physical design of large-scale system-on-chips on advanced process technologies, in collaboration with Cadence. The company is applying that flow to the physical design of a large-scale 3-nanometer SoC, using the Cadence InnoStack AI Super Agent, and plans to expand its use across SoC projects. Retrieval-augmented generation, Model Context Protocol support, customized AI skills, and AI agents are how Socionext says it is putting internal design knowledge into floorplanning, custom timing-analysis checks, and planned checklist automation. President and chief operating officer Hisato Yoshida said the company expects up to 5X overall productivity gains through Cadence's agentic AI workflow. Cadence senior vice president Chin-Chi Teng described the InnoStack agent as open enough for a customer to load its own methodologies. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/socionext-expands-agentic-ai-to-advanced-large-scale-soc-physical-design/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=socionext-expands-agentic-ai-to-advanced-large-scale-soc-physical-design)

**NTT Consortium Developing Mass-Production Tech for Optical Chiplets: Semiconductor Digest**
A consortium advised by NTT is jointly developing mass-production technologies for optical chiplets. The participating companies are the developers; NTT's stated role is advisor. The item is a development program, not a production start. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/ntt-consortium-developing-mass-production-tech-for-optical-chiplets/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=ntt-consortium-developing-mass-production-tech-for-optical-chiplets)

### Data Centres & Power
**Amazon pledges €16bn investment in Germany in 2027: Data Center Dynamics**
Amazon has pledged a €16 billion investment in Germany in 2027. Data Center Dynamics reports that the pledge includes expanding data centers and AI infrastructure, high-speed satellite internet, and logistics. This is a pledged investment year, not an energized site, and the report does not assign the euros to a named campus. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/amazon-pledges-16bn-investment-in-germany-in-2027/)

**Georgia electric cooperative plans 50-MW home battery deployment: Utility Dive**
Central Georgia Electric Membership Corporation plans a 50-megawatt home-battery deployment. Utility Dive reports the batteries are intended to reduce system peaks and energy costs as hyperscale data centers seek to connect to its grid. The 50 megawatts are batteries on the cooperative's system, not a data-center IT load. Source: [utilitydive.com](https://www.utilitydive.com/news/georgia-electric-cooperative-plans-50-mw-home-battery-deployment/833492/)

**OVHcloud has 110MW of data center capacity up for grabs: Data Center Dynamics**
OVHcloud has 110 megawatts of data-center capacity available to grow its customer base, the company said on its annual earnings call, Data Center Dynamics reports. That figure is capacity the operator says it can sell, not a new site breaking ground. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/ovhcloud-has-110mw-of-data-center-capacity-up-for-grabs/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Dell CEO Says the Memory Shortage Will Get Worse in 2027: TechPowerUp**
Michael Dell, Dell's chairman and chief executive, told The Wall Street Journal that the memory shortage will get worse next year as AI data-center buildout keeps absorbing DRAM and high-bandwidth memory. TechPowerUp reports Dell is sitting on roughly $95 billion of AI server orders it has not delivered, which Dell called the largest backlog in its history, and that memory—not demand—is what is holding shipments. Accelerators in those servers need HBM; the servers around them still need conventional DRAM. Dell does not expect meaningful new supply until 2029 or 2030, because new memory fabs take around four years to build. That lines up with comments TechPowerUp attributes to Micron's chief executive, that supply will be much tighter in 2027 and 2028 than this year, and to SK hynix's chief executive, who expects the shortage to last through 2030. Dell is coping by buying DRAM only when final assembly is close and by locking long-term supply agreements. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/353947/dell-ceo-says-the-memory-shortage-will-get-worse-in-2027)

**Micron Invests in New York Critical Minerals Processing With Indium Corporation: Semiconductor Digest**
Micron has announced strategic funding so Indium Corporation can expand refining and high-purity materials manufacturing in Rome, New York, restarting domestic processing of critical minerals used in advanced semiconductor manufacturing. The deal sits inside a plan Micron announced in July to invest up to $3 billion to strengthen the U.S. semiconductor supply chain. The companies will enter a long-term supply agreement giving Micron access to those high-purity minerals, which Micron's chief procurement officer, Ben Tessone, tied to the company's technology roadmap and to reducing reliance on concentrated global refining. Micron also restated plans to increase expected U.S. fab and technology spend to more than $250 billion through 2035. New York Governor Kathy Hochul said the Clay fab investment is months ahead of schedule and called it the largest private investment in New York State history. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/micron-invests-in-new-york-critical-minerals-processing-with-indium-corporation/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=micron-invests-in-new-york-critical-minerals-processing-with-indium-corporation)

**TSMC Plans 3nm Chip Production At Second Japan Factory: Electronics For You BUSINESS**
TSMC plans to manufacture 3-nanometer chips at the second factory of Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing, its Kumamoto joint venture—a plan, not a line in production. Total equipment investment in the venture is expected to exceed $23 billion. TSMC's Japan account said production and investment would be implemented in phases based on market demand and would proceed on the premise of Japanese government support. In August, TSMC and Sony Semiconductor Solutions agreed to a separate Kumamoto joint venture, Advanced Vision Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp., for next-generation image sensors, with commercial production scheduled to begin in 2029, according to Focus Taiwan as cited in the report. Source: [electronicsforyou.biz](https://www.electronicsforyou.biz/industry-buzz/tsmc-plans-3nm-chip-production-at-second-japan-factory/) Source: [timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/tsmc-plans-3nm-semiconductor-manufacturing-at-second-japan-factory-investment-to-exceed-usd-23-billion/articleshow/135079887.cms)

**ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent place over $35 billion worth of Nvidia chip orders: Reuters**
Reuters reports, as an exclusive, that ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent have placed more than $35 billion worth of Nvidia chip orders. The figure is orders placed, not chips described as delivered. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/bytedance-alibaba-tencent-place-over-35-billion-worth-nvidia-chip-orders-2026-10-20/)

### Also Today
**Musk's Terafab Chip Ambition Started With Rejected Bids for Intel, TSMC and Micron Plants: BigGo Finance**
BigGo Finance, citing The Elec, reports Elon Musk approached Intel, TSMC, and Micron to buy existing fabs, was turned down, and shifted Terafab to partnerships, with Intel contributing its 14A process while Musk has limited TSMC to a subcontractor role at most. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/5880d826-c6cb-4bad-afc7-cce78352383c) Source: [wccftech.com](https://wccftech.com/elon-musk-tried-to-buy-chip-plants-from-intel-tsmc-and-micron-before-building-terafab-but-was-snubbed-and-pivoted-to-partnerships-to-fuel-plan-for-million-times-of-earth-economy/)

**South Korea's Ruling Party Lawmaker Slams AI Data Center Grid Code Plan: BigGo Finance**
A ruling-party lawmaker in South Korea has criticized a planned AI data-center grid code and urged an exemption for projects already underway. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/2352c1fc-492d-494b-aca1-71b109bb4271)

**Tens of thousands of Nvidia GPUs sit idle in Meta's Prometheus supercluster: The Register**
The Register reports that tens of thousands of Nvidia GPUs in Meta's Prometheus supercluster sit idle, held ready for a failure. Source: [theregister.com](https://www.theregister.com/systems/2026/10/20/tens-of-thousands-of-nvidia-gpus-sit-idle-in-metas-prometheus-supercluster-just-waiting-for-a-failure/5304269)

**Shadeform launches Flex VMs: Data Center Dynamics**
Data Center Dynamics reports Shadeform's Flex VMs turn bare-metal GPU clusters into single-tenant virtual machines on its marketplace, and that an approved node can be enrolled in about 30 minutes. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/product-news/shadeform-launches-flex-vms-turning-any-bare-metal-gpu-cluster-into-marketplace-ready-cloud-capacity/)

**Contrel, FSE combine laser and plasma processes for advanced packaging: digitimes**
Digitimes reports Contrel and FSE are combining laser and plasma processes for advanced packaging. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20261021PD203/contrel-laser-packaging-high-end-dual-core.html)

**Apple Expands $600 Billion U.S. Manufacturing Plan: Pulse 2.0**
Pulse 2.0 reports Apple is expanding a $600 billion U.S. manufacturing plan with Qnity, Perryman, Broadcom, Corning, Coherent, TSMC, and Amkor. Source: [pulse2.com](https://pulse2.com/apple-expands-600-billion-u-s-manufacturing-plan-with-qnity-perryman-broadcom-corning-coherent-tsmc-and-amkor/)

### The Teardown: Why the Fiber Array Cannot Touch the Die
Co-packaged optics does not become a volume product when the photonic die lights up on a bench. It becomes a volume product when a factory can attach light and electricity at the same time, on every insertion, without destroying the only connector the module will ever trust. Semiconductor Engineering's panel on scaling co-packaged-optics test past a single die puts the constraint in the handling, not in the laser. Fiber alignment is the bottleneck on the optical engine. The fiber array unit is supposed to couple light without ever contacting the device. Crash it during bring-up and the array is damaged; leave contamination on it and the measurement is junk, so cleaning is part of the test cell, not a side chore.

Dave Armstrong of ISE Labs, an ASE Group subsidiary, draws the power line that keeps many insertions at one die. If the main ASIC is an 8-kilowatt GPU, with multiple connectors around multiple sides, tester resources have to deliver that power and pull the heat back out. That combination is hard to extend past one die. Matt Griffin of Teradyne agrees that most production solutions today are single-site, and that multi-site probe cards would relieve the fiber-alignment bottleneck if they work. Ira Leventhal of Advantest treats the connector as the part that will not scale on optimism. A ball-grid array already teaches the same lesson: socket the device too many times and the balls are at risk. The device-side optical connector is designed to be attached once and, the hope is, never disconnected. A test-side connector that survives 20 to 50 insertions is not a production tool. It needs to last for tens of thousands of insertions, or 100,000. The fix the panel describes is a hardened metal on the tester side. That hardened metal then mates to a receptacle on the device that is not hardened. Careless mating can wear out the device connector before the spec lifetime, which means the test method can scrap the part it was built to qualify.

Kazuo Yamaguchi of Keysight separates the easy simultaneous contact from the one that actually characterizes the engine. DC pads plus an optical probe are a mechanical problem. Modulator and photodetector performance is validated through S-parameters, so optical contact and high-frequency radio-frequency contact have to land together. Probe cards fit only a limited number of RF lines, and their bandwidth is limited, while today's devices are characterized beyond 200 gigahertz. At wafer and die insertions, simultaneous connection is an RF probing problem sitting on top of fiber alignment. Leventhal adds warpage: alignment has to hold in multiple axes, either from the top or from the side, while a dense ball-grid array still has to make reliable electrical contact. Griffin's map of the package makes the geometry worse at module level. Every insertion has an optical interface and an electrical interface. Those interfaces can be on the top, the bottom, or both. At module level they can sit on two to four sides of the package, across some number of optical engines. Optical alignment by itself, he says, is not the large challenge. Doing it on every face, at the same time as power and RF, is.

A worked pass through Armstrong's split shows where single-site is still the rational cell and where it stops paying. Take the 8-kilowatt GPU with connectors on several sides. Tester power delivery and heat extraction already strain a one-die insertion, so adding a second site does not buy throughput if the tester cannot feed both parts. Photonic-integrated-circuit wafer test, in his experience, is single-site today, with some hope of moving up if probe-card makers—he names Technoprobe—can put more optical sites on one card. Near-packaged optics, by contrast, is typically a single-connector device. High-volume output of that class forces multi-site, because one connector and one alignment per tester hour will not clear the line. He calls insertions two and three the fertile ground: they are the longer, more complex insertions, and they are where multi-site has room to remove time. Griffin's hope is the same from the optical side. Multi-site fiber alignment is what lets the industry ramp faster. It is not here as a production default.

Single-site remains the right choice while three conditions hold at once: the device under test is an 8-kilowatt-class ASIC whose connector count and power exceed what the tester can deliver to a second die; the optical probe must never touch the die, so each site still needs its own clean fiber array; and the measurement that matters is an electro-optic S-parameter past 200 gigahertz, which a probe card cannot fan out across many RF lines. That choice stops being the right one when the product is a single-connector near-packaged engine headed for high volume, insertions two and three dominate the test time, and a hardened test connector can survive on the order of 100,000 matings without chewing through the softer receptacle on the device. Until that connector and a multi-site fiber card both exist, adding sites multiplies crashes and contamination faster than it multiplies good parts. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/scaling-cpo-testing-beyond-a-single-die/)

### On the Horizon
- Construction of TSMC Fab 22 Phase 4 in Kaohsiung is set to be completed next year, on a site now suspended for steel-structure work.
- Commercial production at Advanced Vision Semiconductor Manufacturing, the TSMC–Sony image-sensor joint venture in Kumamoto, is scheduled to begin in 2029.
- Amazon's pledged Germany investment, including data-center and AI infrastructure expansion, is dated to 2027.
- Dell does not expect meaningful new memory-fab supply until 2029 or 2030.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **One Vera CPU replaces the dual-CPU BlueField-4, giving context-memory servers a cheaper board.**

**What You Need to Know:** One Vera CPU now anchors the BlueField-4 STX context-memory server NVIDIA showed at OCP 2026, a lower-cost board than the dual-Vera design. Intel has asked the FCC for a waiver so foreign automated guided vehicles in its US fabs can keep receiving updates after a July import ban. Manchester Financial Group is exploring a 400-megawatt data centre at a former Navy cyber site in San Diego, while Canada has opened a procurement notice for an Ontario data centre estimated at 1.5 to 1.85 billion Canadian dollars.

### Top Story
NVIDIA showed the BlueField-4 STX server for context memory at OCP 2026, and ServeTheHome describes it as the lower-cost board partners had been asking for. The earlier BlueField-4 paired two Vera CPUs, each with SOCAMM memory, and four ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, closer to a dual-socket server than to a BlueField-1 or BlueField-3 DPU. The STX card is much smaller, uses high-density connectors for PCIe and system links, and carries a Vera-class package rather than an embedded-class DPU CPU. Memory is SOCAMM, so a heatsink or a liquid-cooling block can sit on the package, and an M.2 slot is onboard for what is usually an operating-system drive. A soldered CPU and LPDDR5X, instead of DDR5 DIMM slots, keep the board about the size of an Intel DMR 16-channel socket or a 16-channel AMD EPYC Venice platform, and the layout is meant to be assembled automatically. ServeTheHome did not see a ConnectX-9 SuperNIC on the OCP boards, and notes that NAND prices have been rising meaningfully over the past year. Source: [servethehome.com](https://www.servethehome.com/nvidia-bluefield-4-stx-server-for-cmx-at-ocp-2026/)

### Silicon
**Helios logical memory hits 99.9995 percent: HPCwire**
Quantinuum reported 99.9995 percent logical memory fidelity on its Helios quantum computer, equivalent to roughly five failures per million cycles. Chief executive Rajeeb Hazra told The Wall Street Journal, "This derisks the industry." The company says the result strengthens its path to Apollo, the planned fault-tolerant system. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/2026/10/19/quantinuum-says-helios-results-strengthen-its-path-to-apollo/)

**Vera doubles agent throughput in early Modal tests: Arm**
Arm said Modal's early benchmarks show NVIDIA Vera, built on Arm, delivering up to twice the throughput of comparable x86 systems under heavy concurrency. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Arm/status/2112243854640574880)

**JUPITER hosts a record fault-tolerant quantum simulation: NVIDIA Newsroom**
NVIDIA announced a record quantum-computing simulation on JUPITER, Europe's first exascale supercomputer. The run validated magic-state cultivation, an approach to fault-tolerant quantum computing that requires 90 percent fewer qubits than previous methods. Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-runs-record-simulation-of-fault-tolerant-quantum-computing-at-julich-supercomputing-centre)

**Superconducting neural chip passes a fusion-data test: HPCwire**
A superconducting neural-network chip that borrows techniques from quantum computers passed a battery of tests processing data from a fusion reactor, in work HPCwire ties to the Genesis Mission. Great Sky, Brookhaven National Laboratory, Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory, and the DIII-D National Fusion Facility are partnered on the effort. The chips differ from conventional silicon. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/2026/10/19/superconducting-neuromorphic-chip-passes-fusion-test/) Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/great-sky-national-labs-explore-superconducting-ai-for-plasma-control/)

### Data Centres & Power
**400MW data center eyed at old Navy cyber site in San Diego: Data Center Dynamics**
Manchester Financial Group is exploring a 400-megawatt data centre at the former Navy NAVWAR headquarters in San Diego, California. The figure is a site being eyed, not an energized campus. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/400mw-data-center-eyed-at-old-navy-cyber-site-in-san-diego-california/)

**Canada puts out an advanced procurement notice for an Ontario data centre: Data Center Dynamics**
Canada has announced an advanced procurement notice for a data centre in Ontario, estimated to cost between 1.5 billion and 1.85 billion Canadian dollars. A procurement notice is not a signed build contract. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/canada-puts-out-advanced-procurement-notice-for-data-center-in-ontario/)

**SemiAnalysis holds 195 megawatts going live in 2027: Dylan Patel**
Dylan Patel of SemiAnalysis said there is no correction to the model's figure: 195 megawatts go up in 2027. Crusoe's figures are a bit higher; Patel said the model follows what will actually be built. The capacity is being built now, some of it goes live in 2027, and the model accounts for partial construction of sites. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/dylan522p/status/2112251939702628745) Source: [x.com](https://x.com/dylan522p/status/2112287857180377399)

**Is front-of-the-meter power the next data centre play?: Data Center Knowledge**
Front-of-the-meter power, as Data Center Knowledge defines it, is generation a data-centre operator develops or backs so electricity feeds the grid rather than a single campus. Amazon has been linked to a possible arrangement of that kind at a large AI data centre it is building in Texas, and public statements still have the company exploring rather than committed. The piece distinguishes that from behind-the-meter generation, which serves one facility, and from grid-interactive designs whose on-site plant still exists first to support the data centre. Building or backing a grid-serving plant is capital-intensive, and most operators are still on utility partnerships, long-term procurement, storage, and behind-the-meter generation. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/energy-power-supply/is-front-of-the-meter-power-the-next-data-center-play-)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Intel seeks an FCC waiver to keep foreign fab robots running: BigGo Finance**
Intel filed a waiver request with the FCC on October 16, made public Monday, after Bloomberg's account of the petition. In July the FCC added advanced robotic equipment made outside the United States to its covered list, alongside Wi-Fi routers and drones, barring those products from the US market; gear already in use can stay, but companies can no longer update its hardware, software, or firmware. Intel said its fabs rely on automated guided vehicles long supplied by Japan's Murata Machinery and Daifuku, that no validated US-made alternative meets its standards, and that fully replacing the fleet would take years. The company called continued operation critical to US national security and said a disruption would immediately and negatively affect its US manufacturing capacity, seeking a conditional waiver because it is unclear whether upgrades would violate the rules. TSMC, Micron, GlobalFoundries, Samsung Electronics, and Texas Instruments may need similar waivers; there is no information that they have filed. The covered list has shifted to category-wide controls; Netgear obtained a license in April after the Defense Department found no national-security threat, and AT&T, Verizon, and a broadband association were allowed hardware upgrades on consumer Wi-Fi routers. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/d41f6671-7aad-4986-9cd0-efc912166d3c)

**Qualcomm wins key Arm claims; damages are $2: EE Times**
Qualcomm won key claims against Arm in a four-year intellectual-property dispute, with damages totaling just $2. EE Times says the verdict safeguards Qualcomm's custom processors while putting financial pressure on Arm. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/qualcomm-wins-key-claims-against-arm-but-damages-total-just-2/)

**ESD industry revenue reaches $5,710.8 million in Q2 2026: Semiconductor Digest**
Electronic system design industry revenue rose 12.2 percent to $5,710.8 million in the second quarter of 2026, from $5,089.4 million in the second quarter of 2025, the ESD Alliance, a SEMI technology coalition, reported. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/electronic-system-design-industry-posts-5-7-billion-in-revenue-in-q2-2026-esd-alliance-reports/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=electronic-system-design-industry-posts-5-7-billion-in-revenue-in-q2-2026-esd-alliance-reports)

### Also Today
**HANMI Semiconductor opens HANMI USA: Semiconductor Digest**
HANMI Semiconductor has opened US subsidiary HANMI USA as a step into the US semiconductor market. Source: [semiconductor-digest.com](https://www.semiconductor-digest.com/hanmi-semiconductor-opens-hanmi-usa/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=hanmi-semiconductor-opens-hanmi-usa)

**540 NVIDIA GPUs power a Japanese quantum-HPC system: Quantum Zeitgeist**
Quantum Zeitgeist reports a new quantum-HPC system at a Japanese research institute powered by 540 NVIDIA GPUs. Source: [quantumzeitgeist.com](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/quantum-hpc-system-nvidia-gpus/)

**Russian official proposes data centres in disused coal mines: Data Center Dynamics**
A Russian official has proposed putting data centres in disused coal mines to protect them from drone strikes. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/russian-official-proposes-data-centers-in-disused-coal-mines-to-protect-from-drone-strikes/)

### The Teardown: When the Checkpoint Outgrows the Sky
Thirteen point four trillion particles stay in the calculation only if every tracer's state can sit in memory while the bytes that merely keep the run alive go somewhere else. HPCwire reports that an Argonne team used the Aurora exascale machine at the Argonne Leadership Computing Facility to finish two of the largest cosmological simulations yet run. Each one followed 13.4 trillion dark-matter particles across a region 28.6 billion light-years wide. The code is HACC, the Hardware/Hybrid Accelerated Cosmology Code. Gravity is the only force in these runs. Particles stand in as tracers of dark-matter density and velocity, so the hot state is position and velocity for each tracer, not gas, stars, or radiation.

Aurora is built for that residency. The system has 10,624 nodes and 63,744 GPUs. Each of these runs drew on 8,100 nodes and roughly 50,000 GPUs. The simulations and much of the analysis finished in about four days. High-capacity memory is the constraint the team names: trillions of particles had to stay readily available as the calculation moved. A gravity-only state is what made that volume fit.

The other limit is the restart. A multi-day run on most of the machine cannot assume it finishes in one sitting. Aurora's Distributed Asynchronous Object Storage, DAOS, took the checkpoint stream. The two simulations wrote more than 85 petabytes through DAOS, mostly as restart checkpoints, so an interruption resumes instead of starting over. About 8 petabytes were kept for scientific analysis.

Walk those two write figures. More than 85 petabytes went through DAOS. About 8 petabytes stayed for science. The checkpoint stream is more than ten times the analysis archive. Most of the bytes the runs produced were not the sky. They were the right to continue the sky. Eighty-five against eight is the worked ratio, and it sits on top of the machine split already named: 8,100 nodes out of 10,624, and roughly 50,000 GPUs out of 63,744, for about four days, twice, once for each 13.4-trillion-particle volume.

That cut stops being the right design when the question needs the gas and the stars in the same volume. The same HACC team had already used Frontier for a different cosmology run, a hydrodynamic simulation that added gas, stars, and other galaxy-formation processes, and that effort produced the largest hydrodynamic simulation of the universe to date. Adding those fields multiplies the state per particle. HPCwire is explicit that focusing on gravity alone is what let Aurora hold a larger volume and more particles. When galaxy formation has to live inside the same box as the largest-scale density field, the resident set and the checkpoint both grow, and the gravity-only cut is no longer the run the survey analysis requires. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/argonnes-aurora-supercomputer-powers-2-of-the-largest-cosmological-simulations-to-date/)

### On the Horizon
- Quantinuum still dates Apollo, its planned fault-tolerant system, to 2029.
- A bigger Great Sky chip is slated for more fusion testing next year.
